      async function saveEvidence(targetSelector) {
        const target = $(targetSelector);
        const select = targetSelector === '#evaluation'
          ? $('#build-dataset') : $('#test-run-dataset');
        const datasetId = select ? Number(select.value) : 0;
        if (!datasetId) {
          toast('select a saved dataset before saving evidence.', 'bad');
          return;
        }
        try {
          const data = await call('POST', '/api/test-runs', {
            rule: readRule(),
            dataset_id: datasetId,
            expected_verdict: targetSelector === '#evaluation'
              ? $('#build-expected').value : $('#test-run-expected').value,
            purpose: targetSelector === '#evaluation'
              ? 'manual' : $('#test-run-purpose').value,
            note: targetSelector === '#evaluation'
              ? '' : $('#test-run-note').value,
            rule_entry_id: state.parentId,
          });
          state.selectedTestRunId = data.id;
          if (target) {
            target.classList.remove('stale');
            target.classList.remove('empty');
            renderEvaluation(target, data.result);
          }
          await loadTestRuns();
          toast('Evidence run ' + data.id + ' saved. The rule and dataset hashes are ' +
            'now linked in history.', data.matches_expected === false ? 'bad' : 'good');
        } catch (err) {
          if (!err.handled) throw err;
        }
      }
      
      async function doTestRunSave() {
        await saveEvidence('#test-run-result');
      }
      
      async function doImport() {
        const text = $('#import-text').value;
        const dialect = $('#import-dialect').value;
        if (!text.trim()) { toast('paste a rule first.', 'bad'); return; }
        try {
          const data = await call('POST', '/api/lower',
            {dialect: dialect, text: text});
          state.rule = data.rule;
          state.dialect = dialect;
          state.origin = 'imported';
          state.sourceText = text;
          state.parentId = null;
          $('#dialect').value = dialect;
          writeForm();
          renderOutline($('#import-outline'), data.outline);
          renderMessages($('#import-diagnostics'), data.diagnostics);
          const lost = data.diagnostics.length;
          toast('Loaded into the builder.' + (lost
            ? ' ' + lost + ' thing(s) could not be represented \u2014 they are ' +
              'listed rather than dropped.'
            : ' Everything in it was representable.'), 'good');
          selectTab('build');
          doRender();
        } catch (err) {
          if (!err.handled) throw err;
        }
      }
      
      async function doFromLog() {
        /* The analysis used to run HERE, in the browser: field stability, the
           volatility heuristics and the rule assembly were all JavaScript, which
           made the most consequential decision in the tool -- which fields become
           the detection -- the one decision the Python test suite could not reach.
           It is now `ruleforge/synthesize.py` behind `/api/synthesize`, so there is
           one implementation and it is tested. This function only collects the
           options and renders what comes back. */
        const options = {
          table: $('#log-table').value.trim(),
          skip_volatile: $('#opt-skip-volatile').checked,
          skip_timestamps: $('#opt-skip-timestamps').checked,
          threshold: $('#opt-threshold').checked,
          group_by: linesOf($('#opt-groupby').value.replace(/,/g, '\n')),
        };
        try {
          const data = await call('POST', '/api/synthesize', {
            text: $('#log-text').value,
            format: $('#log-format').value,
            options: options,
          });
          renderFieldAnalysis(data.fields, data.samples);
          renderMessages($('#log-messages'), data.diagnostics);
          state.rule = data.rule;
          state.origin = 'synthesized';
          state.sourceText = $('#log-text').value;
          state.parentId = null;
          writeForm();
          /* The toast says HYPOTHESIS, and the diagnostics panel says which of the
             pinned fields are doubtful. A generated rule that reads like an authored
             one is a generated rule that gets deployed without review. */
          const problems = (data.diagnostics || [])
            .filter(d => d.severity === 'problem').length;
          toast('Proposed a rule from ' + data.samples + ' samples'
                + (problems ? ' with ' + problems + ' thing(s) to check' : '')
                + '. It is a hypothesis \u2014 read the notes before deploying it.',
                problems ? 'bad' : 'good');
          selectTab('build');
          doRender();
        } catch (err) {
          if (!err.handled) throw err;
          /* The field table is cleared on failure. Leaving the previous analysis on
             screen next to a failed run is how an analyst reads one sample's
             results as another's. */
          $('#log-fields').textContent = '';
          renderMessages($('#log-messages'), []);
        }
      }
      
      function renderFieldAnalysis(fields, sampleCount) {
        const host = $('#log-fields');
        host.textContent = '';
        host.appendChild(el('div', 'hint', fields.length + ' fields across ' +
                                          sampleCount + ' samples'));
        const table = el('table', 'grid');
        const head = el('tr');
        ['', 'field', 'values', 'present', 'sample'].forEach(c => {
          head.appendChild(el('th', null, c));
        });
        table.appendChild(head);
        fields.forEach(field => {
          const tr = el('tr');
          const mark = el('td', null, field.include ? 'pin' : '\u2014');
          if (field.include) mark.style.color = 'var(--ok)';
          else mark.classList.add('tag-absent');
          tr.appendChild(mark);
          tr.appendChild(el('td', null, field.name));
          tr.appendChild(el('td', 'num', String(field.distinct)));
          tr.appendChild(el('td', 'num', field.present + '/' + field.total));
          const sample = el('td', null, String(JSON.stringify(field.sample)).slice(0, 40));
          if (field.reasons.length) sample.title = field.reasons.join('; ');
          tr.appendChild(sample);
          table.appendChild(tr);
        });
        host.appendChild(table);
        host.appendChild(el('div', 'hint',
          'Hover a sample value to see why a field was skipped.'));
      }
      
      async function doSave() {
        try {
          const entry = await call('POST', '/api/history', {
            rule: readRule(),
            origin: state.origin,
            source_text: state.sourceText,
            parent_id: state.parentId,
            note: '',
          });
          /* The saved version becomes the parent of the next save, so a tuning
             session reads as a chain rather than as a pile of unrelated rows. */
          state.parentId = entry.id;
          state.origin = 'authored';
          toast('Saved version ' + entry.id + '. The next save will record itself ' +
                'as derived from it.', 'good');
        } catch (err) {
          if (!err.handled) throw err;
        }
      }
      
      async function loadHistory() {
        const params = new URLSearchParams();
        const q = $('#history-q').value.trim();
        if (q) params.set('q', q);
        if ($('#history-origin').value) params.set('origin', $('#history-origin').value);
        if ($('#history-dialect').value) params.set('dialect', $('#history-dialect').value);
        try {
          const data = await call('GET', '/api/history?' + params.toString());
          const host = $('#history-list');
          host.textContent = '';
          if (!data.entries.length) {
            host.appendChild(el('div', 'empty',
              'Nothing saved yet. Save a version from the Build tab.'));
            return;
          }
          data.entries.forEach(entry => {
            const row = el('div', 'entry' +
              (state.selectedEntry === entry.id ? ' sel' : ''));
            row.appendChild(el('span', 'badge ' + entry.origin, entry.origin));
            row.appendChild(el('span', 'e-title',
              entry.title || entry.rule_id || '(untitled)'));
            row.appendChild(el('span', 'e-meta',
              '#' + entry.id + ' \u00b7 ' + entry.dialect + ' \u00b7 ' +
              entry.created_at.replace('T', ' ').replace('+00:00', 'Z')));
            row.onclick = () => openEntry(entry.id);
            host.appendChild(row);
          });
        } catch (err) {
          if (!err.handled) throw err;
        }
      }
      
      async function openEntry(entryId) {
        try {
          const entry = await call('GET', '/api/history/' + entryId);
          const lineage = await call('GET', '/api/history/' + entryId + '/lineage');
      
          state.rule = entry.rule;
          state.dialect = entry.dialect || state.dialect;
          state.parentId = entry.id;
          state.origin = 'authored';
          state.sourceText = entry.source_text || '';
          state.selectedEntry = entry.id;
          $('#dialect').value = state.dialect;
          writeForm();
      
          const host = $('#history-lineage');
          host.textContent = '';
          host.appendChild(el('div', 'hint',
            lineage.lineage.length + ' version(s), oldest first \u2014 the order ' +
            'the tuning happened in.'));
          lineage.lineage.forEach(version => {
            const box = el('div', 'ol-stage');
            const head = el('div');
            head.appendChild(el('span', 'badge ' + version.origin, version.origin));
            head.appendChild(el('span', 'ol-kind',
              ' #' + version.id + ' ' + (version.title || version.rule_id)));
            box.appendChild(head);
            box.appendChild(el('div', 'hint',
              version.created_at.replace('T', ' ').replace('+00:00', 'Z')));
            if (version.note) box.appendChild(el('div', 'ol-expr', version.note));
            if (version.id === entry.id) box.style.borderLeftColor = 'var(--accent)';
            host.appendChild(box);
          });
      
          if (entry.source_text) {
            host.appendChild(el('h3', null, 'as originally pasted'));
            const pre = el('pre', 'code', entry.source_text);
            host.appendChild(pre);
          }
      
          loadHistory();
          toast('Version ' + entry.id + ' loaded into the builder. Saving will ' +
                'record a new version derived from it.', 'good');
        } catch (err) {
          if (!err.handled) throw err;
        }
      }
      
      /* ------------------------------------------------------------------- start */
      
      function bind() {
        /* The primary tabs carry `data-main`, not `data-pane`: clicking Studio
           returns to the section you were last in rather than always to the first
           one, which is what a two-level header has to do to not lose your place. */
        $('#tabs').addEventListener('click', event => {
          const tab = event.target.closest('.tab');
          if (!tab || !event.currentTarget.contains(tab)) return;
          selectTab(tab.dataset.main === 'home' ? 'home' : (state.studioPane || 'build'));
        });
        /* A click on a label that contains a child element still resolves to the
           button, which is how the rail's own tabs were silently unclickable. */
        $('#subtabs').addEventListener('click', event => {
          const tab = event.target.closest('.tab');
          if (!tab || !event.currentTarget.contains(tab)) return;
          selectTab(tab.dataset.pane);
        });
        $('#dialect').onchange = () => {
          state.dialect = $('#dialect').value;
          /* Re-rendered, not left alone. Switching Sentinel to Splunk used to leave
             KQL on screen under a dropdown reading Splunk -- the label contradicting
             the content, which is worse than showing nothing. */
          scheduleRender();
        };
        /* Any edit anywhere in the builder makes the rendered pane stale. Bound on
           the pane rather than on each control, because a new control is added
           every time a stage is added and a per-control binding would miss them --
           which is how the staleness survived: the handlers that existed did not
           cover the inputs created later. */
        const builder = $('#pane-build');
        if (builder) {
          builder.addEventListener('input', event => {
            if (event.target.closest('#events, #events-format')) return;
            scheduleRender();
          });
          builder.addEventListener('change', event => {
            if (event.target.closest('#events, #events-format')) return;
            scheduleRender();
          });
        }
        /* Changing the SAMPLE invalidates the verdict but not the rendered rule --
           the query is unchanged, the evidence it was judged against is not. Bound
           separately so editing a sample does not fire a render round trip. */
        ['#events', '#events-format'].forEach(selector => {
          const node = $(selector);
          if (!node) return;
          const invalidate = () => {
            const verdict = $('#evaluation');
            if (verdict && verdict.innerHTML.trim()
                && !verdict.classList.contains('stale')) {
              verdict.classList.add('stale');
              verdict.insertBefore(
                el('div', 'stale-note',
                   'The sample has changed \u2014 this verdict is about the '
                   + 'PREVIOUS one. Press Run again.'),
                verdict.firstChild);
            }
          };
          node.addEventListener('input', invalidate);
          node.addEventListener('change', invalidate);
        });
        $('#add-stage').onclick = () => {
          const kind = $('#add-stage-kind').value;
          const stages = state.rule.rule.pipeline.v;
          /* Before the Emit, always: a stage after the output is a stage that never
             runs, and the rule would look right while doing something else. */
          const emitAt = stages.findIndex(s => s['@'] === 'Emit');
          const at = emitAt < 0 ? stages.length : emitAt;
          stages.splice(at, 0, newStage(kind, stages.length));
          renderStages();
        };
        $('#render').onclick = doRender;
        $('#validate').onclick = doValidate;
        $('#run').onclick = doRun;
        $('#run-save-evidence').onclick = () => saveEvidence('#evaluation');
        $('#save').onclick = doSave;
        $('#import-go').onclick = doImport;
        $('#log-go').onclick = doFromLog;
        $('#history-refresh').onclick = loadHistory;
        $('#history-q').onkeydown = event => {
          if (event.key === 'Enter') loadHistory();
        };
        $('#history-origin').onchange = loadHistory;
        $('#history-dialect').onchange = loadHistory;
      
        $('#dataset-save').onclick = doDatasetSave;
        $('#dataset-refresh').onclick = loadDatasets;
        $('#dataset-search').onclick = loadDatasets;
        $('#dataset-q').onkeydown = event => {
          if (event.key === 'Enter') loadDatasets();
        };
        $('#build-dataset').onchange = event => {
          state.selectedDatasetId = Number(event.target.value) || null;
        };
        $('#test-run-dataset').onchange = event => {
          state.selectedDatasetId = Number(event.target.value) || null;
        };
        $('#test-run-save').onclick = doTestRunSave;
        $('#test-run-refresh').onclick = loadTestRuns;
      
        /* The start pane. */
        $('#home-example').onclick = loadExample;
        $('#home-blank').onclick = startBlank;
        $('#brand').onclick = () => selectTab('home');
        document.querySelectorAll('.home-cards .card, .home-cta [data-goto]').forEach(card => {
          card.onclick = () => selectTab(card.dataset.goto);
        });
      }
      
      (async function start() {
        bind();
        writeForm();
        try {
          await loadDialects();
          await loadDatasets();
          await loadTestRuns();
        } catch (err) { /* already reported */ }
      })();

> That's 20 files. The screens are the bulk. To keep each screen small, the render approach: each screen module exports `mount(ctx)` returning element or `render(root, ctx)`.
> 
> Simplification for reliable rendering: full re-render of the screen on state change (not granular). Since screens contain inputs, full re-render on every keystroke would lose focus. Solution: inputs update state on `input` with `update(fn, {silent:true})` (no re-render), and use `change` for values that affect derived displays. Actually cleanest: inputs write to state on `input` and do NOT trigger a re-render of the current screen (just mark dirty + debounce render + persist). Re-render only happens on: navigation, explicit actions, or async data load. That avoids focus loss and is simple.
> 
> So `update(fn)` marks dirty, persists, updates chrome (rule bar, status bar, rail counts) and schedules a debounced render. To avoid focus loss, `update(fn, {quiet:false})` — I'll implement: mutations from typing use `update(fn)` which sets a flag `state.ui.typing = true`? Simpler: two functions: `mutate(fn)` (no re-render, updates chrome) and `act(fn)` (re-render). Typing uses mutate; buttons use act.

          def _serve_file(self, path: Path, fallback_type: str = "text/plain") -> None:
              try:
                  data = path.read_bytes()
              except OSError:
                  self._send(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": {
                      "code": "NOT_FOUND",
                      "message": f"{path.name} is not part of this build.",
                      "where": "api",
                  }})
                  return
              guessed, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(path.name)
              self.send_response(HTTPStatus.OK)
              self.send_header("Content-Type", f"{guessed or fallback_type}; charset=utf-8")
              self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
              self.send_header("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
              self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
              self.end_headers()
              self.wfile.write(data)
      
          def _serve_static(self, relative: str) -> None:
              # Resolve and then confirm containment. Checking for ".." in the raw
              # string misses encoded traversal and symlinks; comparing resolved
              # paths does not.
              target = (_STATIC_ROOT / unquote(relative)).resolve()
              try:
                  target.relative_to(_STATIC_ROOT.resolve())
              except ValueError:
                  self._refuse(
                      Refusal(
                          "PATH_OUTSIDE_STATIC",
                          f"`{relative}` resolves outside the static directory.",
                          "api",
                      ),
                      HTTPStatus.FORBIDDEN,
                  )
                  return
              if not target.is_file():
                  self._send(HTTPStatus.NOT_FOUND, {"error": {
                      "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": f"{relative} not found.",
                      "where": "api",
                  }})
                  return
              self._serve_file(target)
      
          # -- routing ----------------------------------------------------------
      
          def _dispatch(self, method: str) -> None:
              parsed = urlparse(self.path)
              route = parsed.path.rstrip("/") or "/"
              params = parse_qs(parsed.query)
      
              try:
                  if method == "GET":
                      if route in ("/", "/index.html"):
                          self._serve_file(_TEMPLATE_ROOT / "index.html", "text/html")
                          return
                      if route.startswith("/static/"):
                          self._serve_static(route[len("/static/"):])
                          return
                      if route == "/api/dialects":
                          self._send(HTTPStatus.OK, self.api.dialects())
                          return
                      if route == "/api/health":
                          self._send(HTTPStatus.OK, {"ok": True})
                          return
                      if route == "/api/history":
                          self._send(HTTPStatus.OK, self.api.history(params))
                          return
                      if route == "/api/datasets":
                          self._send(HTTPStatus.OK, self.api.datasets(params))
                          return
                      dataset_id = _entry_id(route, "/api/datasets/")
                      if dataset_id is not None:
                          self._send(HTTPStatus.OK, self.api.dataset(dataset_id))
                          return
                      if route == "/api/test-runs":
                          self._send(HTTPStatus.OK, self.api.test_runs(params))
                          return
                      run_id = _entry_id(route, "/api/test-runs/")

    @property

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The shape the API hands a dialect picker."""

#: Order is display order: ready dialects first, then planned ones roughly by
#: how cheap they are to add. Sigma is listed first among the planned because
#: it is YAML rather than a language, which makes it the cheapest real proof
#: that the IR is actually vendor-neutral rather than KQL-shaped.
#:
#: Planned entries already carry their `*_attr` names even though nothing can
#: call them yet. The convention is `<verb>_<key>` -- sigma.py exports
#: `lower_sigma`, not `lower` -- and leaving the attrs at their bare defaults
#: would mean that flipping a dialect to ready by setting `module=` alone made
#: it refuse with DIALECT_CAPABILITY_MISSING, looking for `lower` in a module
#: that exports `lower_sigma`. Writing the names down now makes going ready a
#: two-field change: the module and the capability flags. The convention is
#: pinned by tests/test_dialects.py so it cannot quietly drift back.
REGISTRY: Final[dict[str, Dialect]] = {
    d.key: d
    for d in (
        Dialect(
            key="sentinel",
            label="Microsoft Sentinel",
            language="KQL",
            module="kql",
            parse_attr="parse_kql",

{
  "path": "web/static/css/tokens.css",
  "instructions": "Single token system for the rebuilt UI.",
  "content": "/* RuleForge design tokens.\n\n   Every colour in the application is declared here and nowhere else. The other\n   stylesheets use these names, and `tests/test_ui_contract.py` fails if a raw\n   colour literal appears outside this file. Two competing `:root` blocks with\n   different names for the same grey is how the old UI drifted. */\n\n:root {\n  color-scheme: dark;\n\n  /* surfaces, darkest to lightest */\n  --surface-page: #0b0e14;\n  --surface-shell: #0e121a;\n  --surface-rail: #0c1017;\n  --surface-card: #131822;\n  --surface-raised: #1a2231;\n  --surface-sunken: #090c12;\n  --surface-hover: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.045);\n  --surface-active: rgba(88, 141, 255, 0.14);\n  --surface-scrim: rgba(4, 6, 10, 0.66);\n\n  --border-quiet: #1b2231;\n  --border-strong: #2a3446;\n  --border-focus: #588dff;\n\n  --text-primary: #e8ecf3;\n  --text-secondary: #a6b1c4;\n  --text-muted: #6d7889;\n  --text-inverse: #08101f;\n\n  --accent: #588dff;\n  --accent-strong: #7aa6ff;\n  --accent-soft: rgba(88, 141, 255, 0.16);\n\n  --state-ok: #3ecf9a;\n  --state-ok-soft: rgba(62, 207, 154, 0.14);\n  --state-caution: #e9b45a;\n  --state-caution-soft: rgba(233, 180, 90, 0.14);\n  --state-danger: #f2687a;\n  --state-danger-soft: rgba(242, 104, 122, 0.14);\n  --state-uncertain: #b795ff;\n  --state-uncertain-soft: rgba(183, 149, 255, 0.14);\n  --state-info: #6fb4e8;\n  --state-info-soft: rgba(111, 180, 232, 0.14);\n\n  --space-1: 4px;\n  --space-2: 8px;\n  --space-3: 12px;\n  --space-4: 16px;\n  --space-5: 24px;\n  --space-6: 32px;\n  --space-7: 48px;\n\n  --radius-sm: 5px;\n  --radius-md: 8px;\n  --radius-lg: 12px;\n  --radius-pill: 999px;\n\n  --shadow-panel: 0 18px 44px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5);\n  --shadow-card: 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.02);\n\n  --font-sans: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, \"Segoe UI\", Roboto,\n    Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;\n  --font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, \"Cascadia Mono\", Menlo, Consolas,\n    monospace;\n\n  --rail-width: 236px;\n  --topbar-height: 54px;\n  --statusbar-height: 26px;\n  --content-max: 1180px;\n  --fast: 120ms ease;\n}\n"
}

Every edit lands here first, and the screen is\n   redrawn from here. `mutate` is for typing (state changes, screen does not\n   re-render, so the caret stays put); `act` is for buttons (state changes and\n   the screen is redrawn). */\n\nimport { emptyRule } from './ir.js';\n\nconst DRAFT_KEY = 'ruleforge.draft.v1';\nconst DRAFT_VERSION = 1;\n\nexport const state = {\n  doc: {\n    payload: emptyRule(),   // exactly what the API calls `rule`\n    ruleId: 'draft',\n    provenance: 'sentinel', // the dialect it came FROM\n    entryId: null,\n    parentId: null,\n    origin: 'authored',\n    sourceText: '',\n  },\n  ui: {\n    screen: 'start',\n    target: 'sentinel',\n    dirty: false,\n    busy: false,\n    problems: [],\n    lastRequest: null,\n    lastResponse: null,\n    inspected: null,\n    paletteOpen: false,\n    inspectorOpen: false,\n  },\n  status: { health: null, lastVerdict: null, ruleHash: null, datasetHash: null },\n  cache: {\n    dialects: [],\n    datasets: [],\n    runs: [],\n    versions: [],\n  },\n  draftSavedAt: null,\n};\n\nlet renderer = () => {};\nconst chromeListeners = [];\n\nexport function setRenderer(fn) {\n  renderer = fn;\n}\n\nexport function onChrome(fn) {\n  chromeListeners.push(fn);\n}\n\nfunction persist() {\n  try {\n    localStorage.setItem(DRAFT_KEY, JSON.stringify({\n      v: DRAFT_VERSION,\n      at: new Date().toISOString(),\n      doc: state.doc,\n      target: state.ui.target,\n    }));\n    state.draftSavedAt = new Date().toISOString();\n  } catch (err) {\n    /* A full or blocked localStorage must not break editing. null;\n  state.doc.parentId = parentId ?? null;\n  state.doc.ruleId = payload && payload.rule && payload.rule.rule_id\n    ? payload.rule.rule_id.v : 'draft';\n  state.ui.dirty = false;\n  state.status.lastVerdict = null;\n  schedulePersist();\n}\n\nexport const doc = () => state.doc.payload.rule;\n\nexport const stages = () => doc().pipeline.v;\n\nexport const stageById = (id) => stages().find((s) => s.id.v === id) || null;\n\nexport function conditions() {\n  return stages().filter((s) => s['@'] === 'Filter');\n}\n\nexport function nextStageId(kind) {\n  const base = String(kind).toLowerCase();\n  let index = stages().length;\n  let candidate = base + '_' + index;\n  const taken = new Set(stages().map((s) => s.id.v));\n  while (taken.has(candidate)) {\n    index += 1;\n    candidate = base + '_' + index;\n  }\n  return candidate;\n}\n"

> - ANNOTATIONS_NOT_TRANSFERABLE → "The target language cannot carry the rule's title, severity and ATT&CK mapping. The query is right; the paperwork is lost." fix → reference
> - DECLARED_ONLY → "This step is modelled and rendered, but only the vendor's own engine can run it." fix → stages
> - UNDECIDED → "Something could not be decided from the sample, so the verdict is 'could not tell', not 'no match'." fix → test
> - DEFAULT_TABLE → "No table was named, so a default was used." fix → source #read-table
> - COMPARISON_UNDECIDABLE / REGEX_DIALECT_SPECIFIC etc. — render diagnostics.
> - REQUEST_* and CODEC_* and STORE_* error codes → generic messages + where.
> 
> I'll structure table entries as `{plain, fix: {label, href, focus}}`.
> 
> Also `severityFor(code)` default.
>

A local sample cannot reproduce that, so a test ' +\n      'reports it instead of pretending.',\n    fix: { label: 'See the selector', href: '#/rule/draft/source', focus: '#read-selector' },\n  },\n  ANNOTATIONS_NOT_TRANSFERABLE: {\n    plain: 'The target language cannot carry the title, severity and ATT&CK ' +\n      'mapping. The query is correct; the paperwork is lost in translation.',\n    fix: { label: 'Which languages carry it', href: '#/reference' },\n  },\n  DECLARED_ONLY: {\n    plain: 'This step is modelled and rendered, but only the vendor\\'s own ' +\n      'engine can actually run it. A local test cannot evaluate it.',\n    fix: { label: 'See the step', href: '#/rule/draft/stages' },\n  },\n  UNDECIDED: {\n    plain: 'Something in the rule could not be decided from this sample, so ' +\n      'the verdict is \"could not tell\" — not \"no match\".',\n    fix: { label: 'Open the test', href: '#/rule/draft/test' },\n  },\n  DEFAULT_TABLE: {\n    plain: 'No source table was named, so a default was assumed. The row is undecided.',\n    fix: { label: 'Open conditions', href: '#/rule/draft/conditions' },\n  },\n  REGEX_INVALID: {\n    plain: 'A pattern in this rule is not valid in the language being ' +\n      'rendered. Validate ' +\n      'refused the rule rather than shipping it.',\n    fix: { label: 'Open conditions', href: '#/rule/draft/conditions' },\n  },\n  DIALECT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: {\n    plain: 'That language is listed but not implemented yet. Nothing is wrong ' +\n      'with your rule.',\n    fix: { label: 'See what is ready', href: '#/reference' },\n  },\n  DIALECT_CANNOT_PARSE: {\n    plain: 'That language can be rendered but cannot be read back, so a rule ' +\n      'cannot be imported from it.',\n    fix: { label: 'Language matrix', href: '#/reference' },\n  },\n  REQUEST_EMPTY: {\n    plain: 'There was nothing to send. This is a bug in the ' +\n      'page, not in your rule.',\n  },\n  REQUEST_TOO_MANY_EVENTS: {\n    plain: 'That sample has more events than one test accepts. Split it or use ' +\n      'a saved dataset.',\n    fix: { label: 'Open datasets', href: '#/datasets' },\n  },\n  REQUEST_TOO_LARGE: {\n    plain: 'The request body was larger than the server accepts. Split the ' +\n      'sample.',\n  },\n  REQUEST_NOT_JSON: {\n    plain: 'The page sent something the server could not read as JSON.',\n  },\n  CODEC_MALFORMED: {\n    plain: 'The rule payload is not a shape this build can read.',\n  },\n  CODEC_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED: {\n    plain: 'This rule was written by a different schema version. Reading it ' +\n      'anyway would be guessing at what changed.',\n  },\n  STORE_DATASET_CORRUPT: {\n    plain: 'A saved dataset could not be read back. The stored bytes are kept; ' +\n      'nothing was deleted.',\n    fix: { label: 'Open datasets', href: '#/datasets' },\n  },\n  STORE_ENTRY_UNKNOWN: {\n    plain: 'That version is not in the store. It may have been forgotten from ' +\n      'another tab.',\n    fix: { label: 'Open versions', href: '#/versions' },\n  },\n  STORE_PARENT_UNKNOWN: {\n    plain: 'The version this was derived from is no longer stored, so the chain ' +\n      'starts here.',\n  },\n  NOT_FOUND: {\n    plain: 'The server does not serve that path.',\n    fix: { label: 'Run the health check', href: '#/health' },\n  },\n  PATH_OUTSIDE_STATIC: {\n    plain: 'A static file request tried to leave the static directory and was ' +\n      'refused.',\n  },\n  NETWORK: {\n    plain: 'The page could not reach the workbench. Is `python run.py` still ' +\n      'running in its terminal?',\n    fix: { label: 'Run the health check', href: '#/health' },\n  },\n  SERVER_ERROR: {\n    plain: 'The server failed while answering. every failure becomes a visible Problem plus a toast.\n    Screens use this so no rejection is ever silently dropped. */\nexport async function attempt(fn, options) {\n  const opts = options || {};\n  try {\n    return await fn();\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (err && err.handled) return null;\n    const problem = problemFromError(err, opts.context);\n    if (err) err.handled = true;\n    state.ui.problems = state.ui.problems\n      .filter((p) => !(p.code === problem.code && p.message === problem.message));\n    state.ui.problems.push(problem);\n    notifier(problem);\n    act(() => {});\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Jump to the control that fixes a problem, and focus it. */\nexport function applyFix(fix) {\n  if (!fix) return;\n  if (fix.href) {\n    const target = document.querySelector('#screen');\n    window.location.hash = fix.href;\n    if (fix.focus) {\n      /* The screen mounts on the next frame; focus after it exists. */\n      requestAnimationFrame(() => {\n        const node = document.querySelector(fix.focus);\n        if (node) {\n          node.focus();\n          node.scrollIntoView({ block: 'center', behavior: 'smooth' });\n        }\n        void target;\n      });\n    }\n  }\n}\n"

},\n];\n\nexport const GROUPS = ['AUTHOR', 'VERIFY', 'DERIVE', 'REF'];\n\nconst RULE_SCREENS = new Set(\n  ['details', 'source', 'conditions', 'stages', 'preview', 'test'],\n);\n\nexport function byName(name) {\n  return SCREENS.find((s) => s.name === name) || SCREENS[0];\n}\n\nexport function parse(hash) {\n  const raw = String(hash || '').replace(/^#/, '');\n  const [pathPart, queryPart] = raw.split('?');\n  const path = pathPart.split('/').filter(Boolean);\n  const query = new URLSearchParams(queryPart || '');\n\n  if (!path.length) return { name: 'start', query };\n\n  if (path[0] === return '#/' + name + (opts.id ? {
  "path": "web/static/js/core/api.js",
  "content": "/* The HTTP surface: one function per endpoint, one error shape.\n\n   Nothing here interprets a response. The engine's refusals carry a code, a\n   message written for an analyst and a `where`; they are passed through\n   unchanged so the Problems panel can show the engine's own words next to the\n   plain sentence from `problems.js`. */\n\nimport { state } from './state.js';\n\nexport class ApiError extends Error {\n  constructor(code, message, where, severity) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'ApiError';\n    this.code = code;\n    this.where = where;\n    this.severity = severity || 'error';\n  }\n}\n\nasync function request(method, path, body) {\n  const started = performance.now();\n  let response;\n  try {\n    response = await fetch(path, {\n      method,\n      headers: body === undefined ? {} : { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n      body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),\n    });\n  } catch (err) {\n    state.ui.lastRequest = { method, path, at: new Date().toISOString() };\n    state.ui.lastResponse = { transport: 'failed', detail: String(err) };\n    throw new ApiError(\n      'NETWORK',\n      'cannot reach the workbench at ' + location.origin +\n        '. The server may have stopped.',\n      'network',\n    );\n  }\n\n  const text = await response.text();\n  let data = {};\n  if (text) {\n    try {\n      data = JSON.parse(text);\n    } catch (err) {\n      data = { raw: text.slice(0, 400) };\n    }\n  }\n\n  state.ui.lastRequest = {\n    method,\n    path,\n    body: body === undefined ? null : body,\n    status: response.status,\n    ms: Math.round(performance.now() - started),\n    at: new Date().toISOString(),\n  };\n  state.ui.lastResponse = data;\n\n  if (!response.ok) {\n    const error = data.error || {};\n    throw new ApiError(\n      error.code || 'SERVER_ERROR',\n      error.message || ('the server answered ' + response.status + ' with no explanation.'),\n      error.where || 'api',\n      error.severity || (response.status >= 500 ? 'error' : 'error'),\n    );\n  }\n  return data;\n}\n\nconst get = (path) => request('GET', path, undefined);\nconst post = (path, body) => request('POST', path, body);\nconst del = (path) => request('DELETE', path, undefined);\n\n/* -- reads ---------------------------------------------------------------- */\n\nexport const health = () => get('/api/health');\nexport const dialects = () => get('/api/dialects');\n\nexport function history(params) {\n  const query = new URLSearchParams();\n  if (params && params.q) query.set('q', params.q);\n  if (params && params.origin) query.set('origin', params.origin);\n  if (params && params.dialect) query.set('dialect', params.dialect);\n  if (params && params.limit) query.set('limit', params.limit);\n  return get('/api/history?' + query.toString());\n}\n\nexport const entry = (id) => get('/api/history/' + encodeURIComponent(id));\nexport const lineage = (id) => get('/api/history/' + encodeURIComponent(id) + '/lineage');\nexport const forgetEntry = (id) => del('/api/history/' + encodeURIComponent(id));\n\nexport function datasets(q) {\n  const query = new URLSearchParams();\n  if (q) query.set('q', q);\n  return get('/api/datasets?' + query.toString());\n}\n\nexport const dataset = (id) => get('/api/datasets/' + encodeURIComponent(id));\nexport const testRuns = () => get('/api/test-runs');\nexport const testRun = (id) => get('/api/test-runs/' + encodeURIComponent(id));\n\n/* -- rule work ------------------------------------------------------------ */\n\nexport const lower = (dialect, text, ruleId) =>\n  post('/api/lower', { dialect, text, rule_id: ruleId || 'rule' });\n\nexport const render = (dialect, payload) =>\n  post('/api/render', { dialect, rule: payload });\n\nexport const validate = (payload) => post('/api/validate', { rule: payload });\nexport const outline = (payload) => post('/api/outline', { rule: payload });\n\nexport const evaluate = (payload, text, format) =>\n  post('/api/evaluate', { rule: payload, text, format });\n\nexport const synthesize = (text, format, options) =>\n  post('/api/synthesize', { text, format, options });\n\n/* -- writes --------------------------------------------------------------- */\n\nexport const saveVersion = (payload, fields) =>\n  post('/api/history', {\n    rule: payload,\n    origin: fields.origin || 'authored',\n    source_text: fields.sourceText || '',\n    parent_id: fields.parentId ?? null,\n    note: fields.note || '',\n  });\n\nexport const saveDataset = (fields) =>\n  post('/api/datasets', {\n    name: fields.name,\n    description: fields.description || '',\n    format: fields.format || 'jsonl',\n    table: fields.table || 'events',\n    labels: fields.labels || [],\n    text: fields.text,\n  });\n\nexport const saveRun = (fields) =>\n  post('/api/test-runs', {\n    rule: fields.payload,\n    dataset_id: fields.datasetId,\n    expected_verdict: fields.expectedVerdict || '',\n    purpose: fields.purpose || 'manual',\n    note: fields.note || '',\n    rule_entry_id: fields.ruleEntryId ?? null,\n  });\n"
}

{
  "path": "web/static/js/ui/dom.js",
  "content": "/* DOM construction. Nodes only — no innerHTML anywhere, so a rule title\n   containing markup can never become markup. */\n\nexport function h(tag, props, ...children) {\n  const node = document.createElement(tag);\n  if (props) {\n    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(props)) {\n      if (value === null || value === undefined || value === false) continue;\n      if (key === 'class') node.className = value;\n      else if (key === 'text') node.textContent = value;\n      else if (key === 'on') {\n        for (const [event, handler] of Object.entries(value)) {\n          if (handler) node.addEventListener(event, handler);\n        }\n      } else if (key === 'data') {\n        for (const [name, v] of Object.entries(value)) node.dataset[name] = v;\n      } else if (key === 'style') {\n        Object.assign(node.style, value);\n      } else if (key === 'attr') {\n        for (const [name, v] of Object.entries(value)) {\n          if (v !== null && v !== undefined && v !== false) {\n            node.setAttribute(name, v === true ?   "content": "/* The condition editor.\n\n   A condition is an expression tree, not a flat row: `A and (B or C)` is a\n   real thing an analyst writes, and flattening it silently changes the rule.\n   Each node therefore draws itself and asks its parent to replace it — no node\n   needs to know its own address in the tree. */\n\nimport { h } from './dom.js';\nimport { btn } from './components.js';\nimport { touch } from '../core/state.js';\nimport {\n  T, COMPARISON_OPS, boolOp, comparison, describeExpr, fieldRef,\n  fieldRefText, literal, literalFromText, literalToText, newComparison,\n} from '../core/ir.js';\n\nexport function conditionEditor(expr, onChange, options) {\n  const host = h('div', { class: 'cond-list' });\n  renderCondition(host, expr, onChange, options || {});\n  return host;\n}\n\nfunction renderCondition(host, expr, replace, options) {\n  host.textContent = '';\n  if (!expr) {\n    host.appendChild(btn('+ condition', {\n      size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet',\n      onClick: () => { replace(newComparison()); },\n    }));\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const kind = expr['@'];\n\n  if (kind === 'BoolOp') {\n    const wrap = h('div', { class: 'cond-group' });\n    const head = h('div', { class: 'cond-row is-group' });\n    const op = h('button', {\n      class: 'cond-op',\n      type: 'button',\n      title: 'switch between AND and OR',\n      text: expr.op.v.toUpperCase(),\n      on: {\n        click: () => {\n          expr.op = T.str(expr.op.v === 'and' ? 'or' : 'and');\n          touch();\n          renderCondition(host, expr, replace, options);\n        },\n      },\n    });\n    head.appendChild(h('div', { class: 'row' }, op,\n      btn('+', {\n        size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', title: 'add another condition to this group',\n        onClick: () => {\n          expr.operands.v.push(newComparison());\n          touch();\n          renderCondition(host, expr, replace, options);\n        },\n      }),\n      btn('ungroup', {\n        size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet',\n        title: 'collapse this group into a single condition',\n        onClick: () => {\n          /* An empty group is the always-true predicate, which would match\n             everything, so it collapses to its first operand. */\n          replace(expr.operands.v.length ? expr.operands.v[0] : newComparison());\n        },\n      })));\n    head.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'muted mono', text: expr.operands.v.length + ' conditions' }));\n    wrap.appendChild(head);\n\n    expr.operands.v.forEach((operand, index) => {\n      const slot = h('div');\n      renderCondition(slot, operand, (next) => {\n        if (next === null) {\n          expr.operands.v.splice(index, 1);\n          touch();\n          if (expr.operands.v.length === 0) { replace(newComparison()); return; }\n          if (expr.operands.v.length === 1) { replace(expr.operands.v[0]); return; }\n        } else {\n          expr.operands.v[index] = next;\n          touch();\n        }\n        renderCondition(host, expr, replace, options);\n      }, options);\n      wrap.appendChild(slot);\n    });\n    host.appendChild(wrap);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (kind === 'Not') {\n    const wrap = h('div', { class: 'cond-group' });\n    wrap.appendChild(h('div', { class: 'row' },\n      h('span', { class: 'cond-op', text: 'NOT' }),\n      btn('remove not', {\n        size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet',\n        onClick: () => { replace(expr.operand); },\n      })));\n    const slot = h('div');\n    renderCondition(slot, expr.operand, (next) => {\n      if (next === null) { replace(null); return; }\n      expr.operand = next;\n      touch();\n      renderCondition(host, expr, replace, options);\n    }, options);\n    wrap.appendChild(slot);\n    host.appendChild(wrap);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (kind === 'Comparison') {\n    const row = h('div', { class: 'cond-row' });\n\n    const scope = h('select', {\n      class: 'select',\n      'aria-label': 'Which row this field is read from',\n      title: 'left and right are the two sides of a join and mean nothing ' +\n        'outside one',\n    });\n    for (const value of ['current', 'left', 'right']) {\n      const option = h('option', { value, text: value });\n      if (expr.left['@'] === 'FieldRef' && expr.left.scope.v === value) {\n        option.selected = true;\n      }\n      scope.appendChild(option);\n    }\n    scope.onchange = () => {\n      expr.left = fieldRef(fieldRefText(expr.left), scope.value);\n      touch();\n    };\n    row.appendChild(scope);\n\n    const name = h('input', {\n      class: 'input code',\n      type: 'text',\n      value: fieldRefText(expr.left),\n      placeholder: 'win.eventdata.Image',\n      'aria-label': 'Condition field name',\n      on: {\n        change: () => {\n          expr.left = fieldRef(name.value, scope.value);\n          touch();\n        },\n      },\n    });\n    row.appendChild(name);\n\n    const op = h('select', {\n      class: 'select',\n      'aria-label': 'Condition operator',\n    });\n    for (const value of COMPARISON_OPS) {\n      const option = h('option', { value, text: value });\n      if (expr.op.v === value) option.selected = true;\n      op.appendChild(option);\n    }\n    op.onchange = () => { expr.op = T.str(op.value); ', matched without regard to case' : '')\n        : 'numbers are sent as exact decimals, never as floats',\n      on: {\n        change: () => {\n          if (isRegex) {\n            expr.right = {\n              '@': 'Regex',\n              pattern: T.str(value.value),\n              dialect: expr.right.dialect,\n              nocase: expr.right.nocase,\n            };\n          } else {\n            expr.right = literal(literalFromText(value.value));\n          }\n          touch();\n        },\n      },\n    });\n    row.appendChild(value);\n\n    const actions = h('div', { class: 'cond-actions' },\n      btn(expr.negate.v ? ' code' : ''),\n    id: opts.id || null,\n    type: opts.type || 'text',\n    value: opts.value || '',\n    placeholder: opts.placeholder || null,\n    spellcheck: false,\n    autocomplete: 'off',\n    on: {\n      input: () => {\n        const node = document.getElementById(opts.id);\n        mutate(() => { opts.commit(node ? node.value : ''); });\n        if (opts.afterInput) opts.afterInput();\n      },\n      change: opts.onChange,\n    },\n  });\n}\n\nexport function boundTextarea(options) {\n  const opts = options || {};\n  return h('textarea', {\n    class: 'textarea' + (opts.code ? ' code' : ''),\n    id: opts.id || null,\n    rows: opts.rows || 4,\n    placeholder: opts.placeholder || null,\n    spellcheck: false,\n    value: opts.value || '',\n    on: {\n      input: () => {\n        const node = document.getElementById(opts.id);\n        mutate(() => { opts.commit(node ? node.value : ''); });\n      },\n    },\n  });\n}\n\n/* -- annotation helpers --------------------------------------------------- */\n\nexport const mitreToText = () => annotations().mitre_attack.v.map((pair) => {\n  const tactic = pair.v[0].v;\n  const techniques = pair.v[1].v.map((t) => t.v).join(', ');\n  return techniques ? tactic + ': ' + techniques : tactic;\n}).join('\\n');\n\nexport const mitreFromText = (text) => linesOf(text).map((line) => {\n  const colon = line.indexOf(':');\n  const tactic = colon < 0 ? line.trim() : line.slice(0, colon).trim();\n  const techniques = colon < 0 ? []\n    : line.slice(colon + 1).split(',').map((t) => t.trim()).filter(Boolean);\n  return T.tuple([T.str(tactic), T.tuple(techniques.map(T.str))]);\n});\n\nexport const listText = (tuple) => tuple.v.map((item) => item.v).join('\\n');\nexport const listFromText = (text) => T.tuple(linesOf(text).map(T.str));\n\nexport const severityOptions = [\n  { value: '', label: '\\u2014' },\n  { value: 'informational', label: 'informational' },\n  { value: 'low', label: 'low' },\n  { value: 'medium', label: 'medium' },\n  { value: 'high', label: 'high' },\n  { value: 'critical', label: 'critical' },\n];\n\n/** Set the id used in the URL once the rule is saved. */\nexport function noteRuleId(value) {\n  state.doc.ruleId = value || 'draft';\n}\n\nexport { touch };\n"
}

' +\n          'Sentinel calls it a table, Splunk calls it an index.',\n      }),\n      field({\n        label: 'Index-time selector',\n        control: boundText({\n          id: 'read-selector',\n          value: read ? read.selector.v : '',\n          placeholder: 'index=main sourcetype=WinEventLog',\n          code: true,\n          commit: (value) => { if (read) read.selector = T.str(value); },\n        }),\n        hint: 'Narrowing your SIEM applies before any event is read, in that ' +\n          'SIEM\\u2019s own words. Leave blank unless an imported rule had one.',\n      }),\n      field({\n        label: 'Time field',\n        control: boundText({\n          id: 'read-timefield',\n          value: read ? read.time_field.v : '',\n          placeholder: 'TimeGenerated',\n          code: true,\n          commit: (value) => { if (read) read.time_field = T.str(value); },\n        }),\n        hint: 'Required only if the rule counts events over a window.',\n      })),\n  });\n\n  const honesty = card({\n    title: 'Two things this screen cannot do',\n    body: h('div', { class: 'stack' },\n      h('p', { class: 'dim' },\n        'An index-time selector is applied by the SIEM before it reads an ' +\n        'event.   "content": "/* 3 Conditions — the filters, and only the filters.\n\n   The nine other stage kinds live on their own screen. ' filter condition' : ' filter conditions') +\n      ' \\u00b7 a rule with no filter matches every event' }),\n    btn('+ Add condition', { kind: 'primary', onClick: addCondition }));\n\n  const output = outputCard();\n\n  return page('Conditions', {\n    eyebrow: 'Step 3 of 6 \\u00b7 author',\n    sub: 'Every event has to survive all of these, in order. Group conditions ' +\n      'with AND/OR rather than flattening them — a real rule is rarely a list.',\n    actions: [h('span', {\n      class: 'badge',\n      text: state.doc.provenance,\n      title: 'the dialect this rule was read from',\n    })],\n    body: h('div', { class: 'stack-lg' },\n      add,\n      list,\n      output,\n      nextStepFooter('conditions')));\n}\n\nfunction conditionCard(stage) {\n  const pipeline = stages();\n  const index = pipeline.indexOf(stage);\n  const header = h('div', { class: 'split' },\n    h('div', { class: 'row' },\n      h('span', { class: 'stage-kind', text: 'Filter' }),\n      h('span', { class: 'stage-id', text: stage.id.v })),\n    h('div', { class: 'row' },\n      btn('\\u2191', {\n        size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', title: 'move this stage earlier',\n        onClick: () => move(stage, -1),\n      }),\n      btn('\\u2193', {\n        size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', title: 'move this stage later',\n        onClick: () => move(stage, 1),\n      }),\n      btn('duplicate', {\n        size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet',\n        onClick: () => {\n          const copy = structuredClone(stage);\n          copy.id = T.str(nextId('filter'));\n          mutate(() => { pipeline.splice(index + 1, 0, copy); });\n          rerender();\n        },\n      }),\n      btn('\\u00d7', {\n        size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', title: 'remove this filter',\n        onClick: () => {\n          if (pipeline.length <= 2) {\n            toast('a rule with no filter matches every event. Add another ' +\n              'condition before removing this one.', 'bad');\n            return;\n          }\n          mutate(() => { pipeline.splice(index, 1); });\n          rerender();\n        },\n      })));\n\n  return card({\n    title: '',\n    body: h('div', { class: 'stack' },\n      header,\n      conditionEditor(stage.condition, (next) => {\n        mutate(() => { stage.condition = next || newComparison(); });\n        rerender();\n      })),\n  });\n}\n\nfunction emptyState() {\n  const example = comparison('==', fieldRef('EventID'), literal(T.dec('4688')));\n  return h('div', { class: 'stack' },\n    h('div', { class: 'card-body' },\n      h('p', { class: 'dim' },\n        'A filter needs at least one comparison. This is what one looks like:'),\n      h('div', { class: 'cond-row', 'aria-hidden': 'true', style: { opacity: '0.55' } },\n        h('span', { class: 'mono', text: 'current' }),\n        h('span', { class: 'mono', text: 'EventID' }),\n        h('span', { class: 'mono', text: '==' }),\n        h('span', { class: 'mono', text: '4688' }),\n        h('span')),\n      btn('Start from this', {\n        kind: 'primary',\n        onClick: () => {\n          const pipeline = stages();\n          /* A run of filters is a natural AND: insert before the output. */\n          const emitAt = pipeline.findIndex((s) => s['@'] === 'Emit');\n          const filter = newStage('Filter', pipeline.length);\n          filter.condition = example;\n          mutate(() => {\n            pipeline.splice(emitAt < 0 ? pipeline.length : emitAt, 0, filter);\n          });\n          rerender();\n        },\n      })),\n    h('p', { class: 'field-hint', text: 'It is placed immediately before the ' +\n      'output stage, where filters always run.' }));\n}\n\nfunction outputCard() {\n  const emit = stages().find((s) => s['@'] === 'Emit');\n  return card({\n    title: 'Output',\n    sub: 'Every rule ends in exactly one output stage. Everything in it was representable.', 'good');\n    rerender();\n  }, { context: 'explain' });\n}\n\nfunction adopt() {\n  loadRule({\n    payload: outcome.payload,\n    provenance: dialect,\n    origin: 'imported',\n    sourceText: text,\n    entryId: null,\n    parentId: null,\n  });\n  state.ui.target = dialect;\n  toast('Loaded into the editor as an imported rule. Running POST /api/history would write data — unacceptable. So: GET handlers (9) + a set of POST endpoints exercised safely:

There is no fourth answer, and no \"probably\".',\n    body: h('div', { class: 'stack' },\n      verdictRow('matched', 'The rule was answered: at least one event survived ' +\n        'every stage.'),\n      verdictRow('no_match', 'The rule was answered: every event was dropped. One undecided row ' +\n        'makes the whole verdict \"could not tell\", because a confident no built ' +\n        'on a missing field is a false answer.')),\n  });\n\n  const origins = card({\n    title: 'Where a rule came from',\n    body: h('div', { class: 'stack' },\n      h('div', { class: 'row' }, badge('authored', 'authored'),\n        h('span', { class: 'dim', text: 'Written or edited here. 'yes' : 'no',\n        ]),\n      })\n      : h('p', { class: 'muted', text: 'Loading the catalogue\\u2026' }),\n    foot: state.cache.dialects.some((d) => d.note)\n      ? h('span', {}, 'Caveats: ' + state.cache.dialects.filter((d) => d.note)\n        .map((d) => d.key + ' \\u2014 ' + d.note).join(' \\u00b7 '))\n      : null,\n  });\n\n  const codes = card({\n    title: 'Every code this tool can show you',\n    sub: 'A machine code, the sentence it means, and what to do about it. 'ok' : 'fail' }),\n        h('span', { class: 'health-note', text: step.note || '' }),\n        h('span', { class: 'trace-counts', text: step.ms + ' ms' })))),\n    selfTest.verdict !== 'matched'\n      ? h('p', { class: 'problem-plain', text:\n        'Expected \"matched\" from EventID == 4624 against {\"EventID\": 4624}. A ' +\n        'different verdict means the evaluate path changed, not that your rule is wrong.' })\n      : null);\n}\n\nfunction storeCard() {\n  const counts = storeCounts;\n  return card({\n    title: 'What is stored locally',\n    body: counts\n      ? h('div', { class: 'row wrap' },\n        badge(counts.datasets + ' datasets', 'info'),\n        badge(counts.runs + ' receipts', 'info'),\n        badge(counts.versions + ' versions', 'info'),\n        h('span', { class: 'muted', text: 'in data/history.sqlite3' }))\n      : h('p', { class: 'muted', text: 'Loading counts\\u2026' }),\n  });\n}\n\nfunction reproduceCard() {\n  return card({\n    title: 'Reproduce any of this by hand',\n    body: codeBlock({\n      label: 'the same calls, from a terminal',\n      copy: true,\n      text: [\n        '# start the workbench',\n        'python run.py',\n        '',\n        '# does the server answer at all',\n        'curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/health',\n        '',\n        '# the whole engine suite (1,345 tests, no dependencies)',\n        'python run.py verify',\n        '',\n        '# one raw request, exactly as the page sends it',\n        \"curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/render \\\\\",\n        \"  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\\\",\n        \"  -d '{\\\"dialect\\\": \\\"splunk\\\", \\\"rule\\\": {\\\"schema\\\": 1, \\\"rule\\\": {}}}'\",\n      ].join('\\n'),\n    }),\n    foot: h('span', {}, 'The second command proves the engine; the first proves ' +\n      'the page can reach it. When the UI looks wrong, knowing which of those ' +\n      'two broke is most of the diagnosis.'),\n  });\n}\n\nasync function timed(name, fn) {\n  const started = performance.now();\n  try {\n    const detail = await fn();\n    return {\n      name, state: 'ok', ms: Math.round(performance.now() - started),\n      note: detail || '', detail: detail || '',\n    };\n  } catch (err) {\n    return {\n      name, state: 'failed', ms: Math.round(performance.now() - started),\n      note: (err.code || 'ERROR') + ' \\u2014 ' + err.message,\n      detail: err.message,\n    };\n  }\n}\n\nasync function runChecks(explicit) {\n  if (running) return;\n  running = true;\n  rows = [];\n  selfTest = null;\n  if (explicit) rerender();\n\n  const payload = (await attempt(() => api.lower('sentinel', RULE, 'health'),\n    { context: 'health' })) || null;\n\n  const checks = [\n    ['GET /api/health', async () => (await api.health()).ok ? 'ok: true' : 'unexpected body'],\n    ['GET /api/dialects', async () => {\n      const data = await api.dialects();\n      return data.dialects.length + ' dialects, ' +\n        data.dialects.filter((d) => d.status === 'ready').length + ' ready';\n    }],\n    ['GET /api/datasets', async () => (await api.datasets('')).datasets.length + ' rows'],\n    ['GET /api/test-runs', async () => (await api.testRuns()).test_runs.length + ' rows'],\n    ['GET /api/history', async () => (await api.history({ limit: 1 })).entries.length + ' rows'],\n    ['POST /api/lower', async () => payload\n      ? 'parsed, ' + (payload.diagnostics || []).length + ' diagnostic(s)'\n      : 'parsed'],\n    ['POST /api/outline', async () => payload\n      ? ((await api.outline(payload.rule)).outline ? 'outline returned' : 'no outline')\n      : 'skipped: lower failed'],\n    ['POST /api/render', async () => payload\n      ? (await api.render('sentinel', payload.rule)).text.length + ' chars'\n      : 'skipped: lower failed'],\n    ['POST /api/validate', async () => payload\n      ? ((await api.validate(payload.rule)).ok ? 'valid' : 'not valid')\n      : 'skipped: lower failed'],\n    ['POST /api/evaluate', async () => payload\n      ? (await api.evaluate(payload.rule, SAMPLE, 'jsonl')).verdict\n      : 'skipped: lower failed'],\n    ['POST /api/synthesize', async () => {\n      const data = await api.synthesize(SAMPLE + '\\n' + SAMPLE.replace('HEALTH', 'HEALTH2'),\n        'jsonl', {});\n      return data.samples + ' samples, ' + (data.fields || []).length + ' fields';\n    }],\n  ];\n\n  for (const [name, fn] of checks) {\n    rows.push(await timed(name, fn));\n    rerender();\n    void explicit;\n  }\n\n  /* The three write endpoints are listed, not probed: running them would put\n   test rows in the user's store, which is exactly the kind of side effect a\n   health check must not have. */\n  for (const name of ['POST /api/datasets', 'POST /api/history', 'POST /api/test-runs']) {\n    rows.push({\n      name, state: 'skipped', ms: null,\n      note: 'not run: this endpoint writes to your store',\n    });\n  }\n\n  selfTest = await runSelfTest(payload);\n  const counts = await attempt(async () => ({\n    datasets: (await api.datasets('')).datasets.length,\n    runs: (await api.testRuns()).test_runs.length,\n    versions: (await api.history({ limit: 1 })).total || 0,\n  }), { context: 'health' });\n  storeCounts = counts;\n  state.status.health = rows.every((r) => r.state !== 'failed');\n  running = false;\n  rerender();\n}\n\nasync function runSelfTest(lowered) {\n  const steps = [];\n  const step = async (name, fn) => {\n    const started = performance.now();\n    try {\n      const note = await fn();\n      steps.push({ name, ok: true, note: note || '', ms: Math.round(performance.now() - started) });\n    } catch (err) {\n      steps.push({\n        name, ok: false, note: (err.code || 'ERROR') + ' \\u2014 ' + err.message,\n        ms: Math.round(performance.now() - started),\n      });\n    }\n  };\n\n  let rulePayload = null;\n  await step('lower a known rule', async () => {\n    if (!lowered) throw new Error('lower failed above');\n    rulePayload = lowered.rule;\n    return 'parsed';\n  });\n  await step('render it for Sentinel', async () => {\n    const data = await api.render('sentinel', rulePayload);\n    return data.text.split('\\n')[0];\n  });\n  let verdict = null;\n  await step('evaluate one known event', async () => {\n    const result = await api.evaluate(rulePayload, SAMPLE, 'jsonl');\n    verdict = result.verdict;\n    return result.verdict;\n  });\n\n  return {\n    ok: steps.every((s) => s.ok) && verdict === 'matched',\n    verdict: verdict || 'not run',\n    steps,\n  };\n}\n"

'The source is edited on the Source screen.'\n    : kind === 'Filter'\n      ? 'Filters are edited on the Conditions screen.'\n      : null;\n\n  const head = h('div', { class: 'stage-head' },\n    h('span', { class: 'stage-kind', text: kind }),\n    h('span', { class: 'stage-id', text: stage.id.v }),\n    stage.capability && stage.capability.v === 'declared_only'\n      ? badge('appliance only', 'declared')\n      : null,\n    h('span', { class: 'grow' }),\n    kind !== 'Emit'\n      ? h('div', { class: 'row' },\n        btn('\\u2191', {\n          size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', title: 'move earlier',\n          onClick: () => move(index, -1),\n        }),\n        btn('\\u2193', {\n          size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', title: 'move later',\n          onClick: () => move(index, 1),\n        }),\n        btn('\\u00d7', {\n          size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', title: 'remove this stage',\n          onClick: () => remove(index),\n        }))\n      : null);\n\n  const body = h('div', { class: 'stage-body' });\n  const node = h('div', { class: 'stage-card' + (kind === 'Emit' ? /* The rule bar and status bar follow every edit without redrawing the\n       screen, so typing never loses the caret. */\n    refreshShell();\n  });\n}\n\nboot();\n"

```
"""RuleForge -- one entry point for the whole tool.

The pipeline every dialect plugs into:

    parse    native text  -> parsed structure
    lower    parsed       -> Rule          (the model in ir.py)
    render   Rule         -> native text

Nothing above the engine is allowed to know a vendor's syntax, and nothing
in the engine is allowed to know a vendor exists. That is what makes eight
dialects possible without eight tools, and it is enforced by a test rather
than by good intentions.

    python run.py                  open the browser workbench
    python run.py verify           the test suite, then the corpus sweep
    python run.py corpus --full    every corpus rule, with its message
    python run.py check sigma rule.yml

This file is the only entry point. Every other tool in the suite starts with
`python run.py`, and a tool that starts differently is a tool nobody remembers
how to start. It also gives the two things that were only reachable by
remembering a long command: the whole test suite, and the corpus sweep that
the suite does not run.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO

* IT DOES NOT BIND 0.0.0.0 BY DEFAULT. This endpoint parses untrusted rule
  text and evaluates rules against untrusted samples, so it is loopback only
  and says so out loud if you override that.
* IT DOES NOT PRINT A DIFFERENT PORT THAN THE ONE IT SERVES. If the preferred
  port is busy it names the one it actually bound.
* IT DOES NOT NEED ANYTHING INSTALLED. `verify` runs unittest, not pytest,
  because a check that needs a dependency cannot run in the locked-down SOC
  this tool is built for. pytest works too; it is just not the floor.
"""

= 0;\nconst pending = new Map();\nconst consoleErrors = [];\n\nws.addEventListener('message', (event) => {\n  const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n  if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) {\n    const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(msg.id);\n    pending.delete(msg.id);\n    if (msg.error) reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error)));\n    else resolve(msg.result);\n  }\n  if (msg.method === 'Runtime.exceptionThrown') {\n    consoleErrors.push(msg.params.exceptionDetails.exception?.description\n      || msg.params.exceptionDetails.text);\n  }\n  if (msg.method === """The rule history store.

The behaviour worth protecting here is that history is APPEND-ONLY and that
lineage survives. A store that silently overwrote a rule, or lost the link
between a pasted rule and the tuned version of it, would still pass a naive
"can I save and load" test -- so most of these tests are about the second save,
not the first.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from engine.codec import SCHEMA_VERSION
from engine.ir import (
    Annotations,
    Comparison,
    Emit,
    FieldRef,
    Filter,
    Literal,
    Read,
    Rule,
)
from engine.store import ORIGINS, Entry, RuleStore, default_store_path
from engine.values import Refusal


def rule(rule_id="r", title="", threshold=1, dialect="sentinel") -> Rule:
    return Rule(
        rule_id=rule_id,
        pipeline=(
            Read(id="src", table="SecurityEvent"),
            Filter(id="f", condition=Comparison(
                ">=", FieldRef("Hits"), Literal(Decimal(threshold)))),
            Emit(id="out"),
        ),
        annotations=Annotations(title=title),
        metadata={"dialect": dialect, "language": "KQL", "artifact": "rule"},
__init__.py
__pycache__
test_api.py
test_chronicle.py
test_cli.py
test_codec.py
test_common.py
test_core.py
test_corpus_semantics.py
test_crowdstrike.py
test_dialects.py
test_elastic.py
test_fidelity.py
test_industry_complex_pack.py
test_kql.py
test_pipeline.py
test_qradar.py
test_sigma.py
test_splunk.py
test_store.py
test_synthesize.py
test_validate.py
test_wazuh.py

{
  "path": "tests/test_ui_contract.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"The rebuilt front end's contract with itself.\n\nThere is no DOM in this suite, so these tests protect the things that can be\nchecked from bytes on disk -- and those are exactly the things that rot\nsilently: a screen that is not wired, a colour that bypasses the token system, a\ncontrol the redesign quietly dropped, and a template that no longer parses.\n\nThe behavioural checks (a click produces the right request) live in the manual\nacceptance run described in UI_REBUILD_PLAN.md; these are the floor that runs\nwith `python run.py verify`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport unittest\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nWEB = ROOT / \"web\"\nTEMPLATES = WEB / \"templates\"\nSTATIC = WEB / \"static\"\nJS = STATIC / \"js\"\n\nSHELL = TEMPLATES / \"index.html\"\nCLASSIC = TEMPLATES / \"classic.html\"\nTOKENS = STATIC / \"css\" / \"tokens.css\"\n\nSCREENS = [\n    \"start\", \"details\", \"source\", \"conditions\", \"stages\", \"preview\",\n    \"test\", \"datasets\", \"receipts\", \"versions\", \"explain\", \"draft\",\n    \"reference\", \"health\",\n]\n\n#: The old ids that are deliberately gone. Four controls were replaced or\n#: absorbed by the redesign; the rest are the chrome of the old single page\n#: (its panes, its two-level tab bar and the decorative landing-page radios),\n#: which no longer exists because every screen is a URL now.\nRETIRED_IDS = {\n    # the ten-way stage dropdown, replaced by the Stage library's cards\n    \"add-stage\", \"add-stage-kind\",\n    # the three run-and-save paths, collapsed into Receipts\n    \"run-save-evidence\", \"build-dataset\", \"build-expected\",\n    \"build-evidence-status\",\n    # the old page chrome\n    \"tabs\", \"subtabs\", \"current-context\",\n    \"pane-home\", \"pane-build\", \"pane-import\", \"pane-fromlog\",\n    \"pane-datasets\", \"pane-testruns\", \"pane-history\",\n    \"rf-d-sigma\", \"rf-d-splunk\", \"rf-d-sentinel\", \"rf-d-qradar\",\n}\n\n\ndef read(path: Path) -> str:\n    return path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef all_js() -> str:\n    return \"\".join(read(path) for path in sorted(JS.rglob(\"*.js\")))\n\n\nclass Shell(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_the_shell_is_the_shell_and_nothing_else(self):\n        shell = read(SHELL)\n        for mount in (\"id=\\\"rail\\\"\", \"id=\\\"screen\\\"\", \"id=\\\"problems\\\"\",\n                      \"id=\\\"statusbar\\\"\", \"id=\\\"rulebar\\\"\", \"id=\\\"steps\\\"\"):\n            self.assertIn(mount, shell)\n        # A shell that carries markup for a screen has gone back to being a\n        # page with panes, which is what this rebuild was for.\n        self.assertLess(len(shell.splitlines()), 140)\n\n    def test_every_stylesheet_is_linked_in_order(self):\n        shell = read(SHELL)\n        order = [\"tokens.css\", \"base.css\", \"components.css\", \"screens.css\"]\n        positions = [shell.index(name) for name in order]\n        self.assertEqual(positions, sorted(positions))\n\n    def test_the_shell_loads_the_entry_module(self):\n        self.assertIn('type=\"module\" src=\"/static/js/main.js\"', read(SHELL))\n\n    def test_the_old_interface_is_still_reachable(self):\n        # A screen that calls\n        `document.querySelector('#rule-id')` for a value would reintroduce it.\n        \"\"\"\n        patterns = [\n            r\"document\\.querySelector\\('#an-(?:title|description|severity|author)'\\)\",\n            r\"document\\.querySelector\\('#rule-id'\\)\",\n            r\"document\\.querySelector\\('#read-(?:table|selector|timefield)'\\)\",\n        ]\n        for path in sorted((JS / \"screens\").glob(\"*.js\")):\n            source = read(path)\n            for pattern in patterns:\n                with self.subTest(file=path.name, pattern=pattern):\n                    self.assertIsNone(re.search(pattern, source))\n\n\nclass Styling(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_no_colour_lives_outside_the_token_file(self):\n        token_text = read(TOKENS)\n        hex_pattern = re.compile(r\"#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\\b\")\n        self.assertTrue(hex_pattern.search(token_text),\n                        \"the token file should declare the palette\")\n        for path in sorted((STATIC / \"css\").glob(\"*.css\")):\n            if path == TOKENS:\n                continue\n            with self.subTest(file=path.name):\n                self.assertIsNone(\n                    hex_pattern.search(read(path)),\n                    f\"{path.name} declares a raw colour; use a token instead\",\n                )\n\n    def test_every_token_used_is_defined(self):\n        defined = set(re.findall(r\"--[a-z0-9-]+\", read(TOKENS)))\n        used: set[str] = set()\n        for path in sorted((STATIC / \"css\").glob(\"*.css\")):\n            used |= set(re.findall(r\"var\\((--[a-z0-9-]+)\", read(path)))\n        missing = sorted(used - defined - {\"--x\"})\n        self.assertEqual(missing, [], f\"undefined custom properties: {missing}\")\n\n    def test_there_is_only_one_token_block(self):\n        self.assertEqual(read(TOKENS).count(\":root\"), 1)\n        for path in sorted((STATIC / \"css\").glob(\"*.css\")):\n            if path == TOKENS:\n                continue\n            with self.subTest(file=path.name):\n                self.assertNotIn(\":root\", read(path))\n\n\nclass NoMarkupFromStrings(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_the_ui_builds_nodes_never_markup(self):\n        \"\"\"A rule title is user text. Building screens with innerHTML would put\n        it in the document as markup. Every node is created with createElement.\"\"\"\n        sources = list(JS.rglob(\"*.js\"))\n        self.assertTrue(sources)\n        for path in sorted(sources):\n            source = read(path)\n            with self.subTest(file=path.name):\n                self.assertNotIn(\"innerHTML\", source)\n                self.assertNotIn(\"outerHTML\", source)\n                self.assertNotIn(\"insertAdjacentHTML\", source)\n                self.assertNotIn(\"document.write\", source)\n\n\nclass Migration(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_no_control_was_dropped_without_saying_so(self):\n        old = set(re.findall(r'\\bid=\"([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)\"', read(CLASSIC)))\n        new = read(SHELL) + all_js()\n        missing = {\n            name for name in old\n            if f'\"{name}\"' not in new and f\"'{name}'\" not in new\n        }\n        self.assertEqual(\n            sorted(missing - RETIRED_IDS), [],\n            \"these ids vanished from the old UI without being declared retired\",\n        )\n\n    def test_the_retired_list_is_not_a_wish_list(self):\n        \"\"\"Every id declared retired must actually be gone, or the list stops\n        being a record of what happened and becomes a place to hide things.\"\"\"\n        old = set(re.findall(r'\\bid=\"([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)\"', read(CLASSIC)))\n        new = read(SHELL) + all_js()\n        resurrected = sorted(\n            name for name in RETIRED_IDS\n            if name in old and (f'\"{name}\"' in new or f\"'{name}'\" in new)\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(resurrected, [])\n\n\nclass Templates(unittest.TestCase):\n    def test_templates_are_parsed_by_the_engine_they_rely_on(self):\n        \"\"\"A template that no longer lowers is worse than no template.\"\"\"\n        from web.api import Api\n\n        source = read(JS / \"core\" / \"ir.js\")\n        block = source[source.index(\"export const TEMPLATES\"):]\n        dialect = re.findall(r\"dialect: '([a-z]+)'\", block)\n        texts = re.findall(r\"text: \\[(.*?)\\]\\.join\\('\\\\n'\\)\", block, re.S)\n        self.assertEqual(len(dialect), 4)\n        self.assertEqual(len(texts), 4)\n\n        api = Api.__new__(Api)  # lowering needs no store\n        for key, chunk in zip(dialect, texts):\n            body = \"\\n\".join(\n                re.findall(r\"'((?:[^'\\\\]|\\\\.)*)'\", chunk)\n            ).encode().decode(\"unicode_escape\")\n            with self.subTest(template=body.splitlines()[0]):\n                lowered = api.lower({\"dialect\": key, \"text\": body})\n                self.assertIn(\"rule\", lowered)\n                self.assertIn(\"pipeline\", lowered[\"rule\"][\"rule\"])\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    unittest.main()\n"

    def test_the_example_actually_lowers_and_renders(self):
        # The guard that matters: if the example stops loading, the first
        # thing a new user does is see an error.
        import re

        source = self._app_js()
        block = re.search(
            r"const EXAMPLE_RULE = \[([\s\S]*?)\]\.join\('\\n'\);", source
        )
        self.assertIsNotNone(block, "the example text could not be located")
        lines = re.findall(r"'((?:[^'\\]|\\.)*)'", block.group(1))
        text = "\n".join(l.replace("\\\\", "\\").replace("\\'", "'")
                         for l in lines)
        dialect = re.search(
            r"const EXAMPLE_DIALECT = '(\w+)'", source
        ).group(1)

        status, body = self.post(
            "/api/lower", {"dialect": dialect, "text": text}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("rule", body)
        status, rendered = self.post(
            "/api/render", {"dialect": dialect, "rule": body["rule"]}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertTrue(rendered["text"].strip())

class OverHttp(unittest.TestCase):
    """A real socket. Routing, traversal and body limits only exist here."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.store = RuleStore(":memory:")
        cls.server = build_server("127.0.0.1", 0, cls.store)
        cls.port = cls.server.server_address[1]
        cls.thread = threading.Thread(target=cls.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        cls.thread.start()

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.server.shutdown()
        cls.server.server_close()
        cls.thread.join(timeout=5)
        cls.store.close()

    def url(self, path):
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}{path}"

    def get(self, path):
        with urllib.request.urlopen(self.url(path), timeout=10) as response:
            return response.status, json.loads(response.read() or b"{}")

    def post(self, path, payload):
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            self.url(path),
            data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            method="POST",
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
            return response.status, json.loads(response.read() or b"{}")

    def expect_error(self, method, path, payload=None, raw=None):
        if raw is not None:
            request = urllib.request.Request(
                self.url(path), data=raw, method=method,
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            )
        else:
            data = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
            request = urllib.request.Request(self.url(path), data=data, method=method)
        try:
            urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as err:
            return err.code, json.loads(err.read() or b"{}")
        self.fail(f"{method} {path} was expected to fail")

    # -- happy paths ------------------------------------------------------

    def test_health(self):
        status, body = self.get("/api/health")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertTrue(body["ok"])

    def test_the_gui_is_served_at_the_root(self):
        with urllib.request.urlopen(self.url("/"), timeout=10) as response:
            self.assertEqual(response.status, 200)
            self.assertIn("text/html", response.headers["Content-Type"])
            self.assertIn(b"RuleForge", response.read())
