The rebuild is done and running. Here's what landed.

## What you have now

Open `python run.py` → `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. The old interface is untouched at `/classic`.

**14 screens, all visible in one rail, four groups:**

```
AUTHOR   Start · 1 Details · 2 Source · 3 Conditions · 4 Stage library · 5 Preview
VERIFY   6 Test · Datasets · Receipts · Versions
DERIVE   Explain a rule · Draft from logs
REF      Reference · Health
```

Plus the frame that makes problems findable: a **rule bar** (title · id · condition count · unsaved dot), a **step rail** across the authoring screens, a **Problems panel** where every engine code gets a plain sentence and a button that jumps to the control that fixes it, a **status bar** (server · target · rule hash · dataset hash · verdict), `Ctrl+K` jump palette, `Ctrl+Shift+D` state inspector showing the exact payload each request sends.

## The architectural fix, not a repaint

- **One state object** (`core/state.js`). Inputs dispatch; nothing reads the DOM back. `readRule()` is gone.
- **Every screen is a URL** (`#/rule/draft/conditions`), so a broken state can be linked, reloaded, reproduced.
- **One button per verb**: one Render, one Validate, one Test (no save), one save-run (Receipts only), one save-version.
- **Nothing hidden**: the ten stage kinds are ten cards with forms and worked examples, not one dropdown.
- **Nodes, never markup**: no `innerHTML` anywhere — a rule title can't become HTML.
- **One token file.** 78 raw hex literals are down to a single semantic palette; a test fails if a colour appears anywhere else.

## Verified, not assumed

- Real browser, real clicks (CDP): template → edit → Preview renders → **Matched / No match / Could not tell** all three verdicts correct → save version → save dataset → save receipt → lineage → Health. **Zero console errors, zero problems.**
- Health screen exercises 15 handlers and the full lower→render→evaluate chain; the 4 write endpoints are listed as "not run: this endpoint writes to your store" rather than probed.
- `python -m pytest tests` → **1366 passed**. `tests/test_ui_contract.py` is new (19 tests): shell, wiring, id migration, no raw colours, undefined tokens, no markup-from-strings, and the four Start templates actually lowering through the engine.
- I moved 4 pre-existing assertions that described the old markup to the classic page (still served) rather than deleting them.

## Deliberate deviations

- **P6 not done**: `/classic` and `app.js`/`app.css` stay until you've used the new UI and said it's better.
- Stage cards link to Preview instead of embedding a per-stage render — a single stage isn't a rule, and a fake "rendered form" would be a lie.

One thing to know: the 4 extra filters you add with *Add condition* start as `FieldName == ""`, which makes the rule *undecided*, not *no match*. The row now carries a **placeholder** badge so that's visible where it happens.

- path: web\templates\index.html
  content: |
      <!DOCTYPE html>
      <!--
        RuleForge: a local detection-rule workbench.
      
        This file is the shell and nothing else. Every screen is built in
        web/static/js/screens/, every colour is declared in web/static/css/tokens.css,
        and the rule being edited lives in one state object (core/state.js). There is
        no build step and no dependency: the server serves these files off disk,
        which is what lets the tool run inside a locked-down SOC.
      -->
      <html lang="en">
      <head>
      <meta charset="utf-8">
      <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
      <title>RuleForge</title>
      <link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/css/tokens.css">
      <link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/css/base.css">
      <link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/css/components.css">
      <link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/css/screens.css">
      </head>
      <body>
      
      <div class="app">
      
        <header class="topbar">
          <a class="brand" href="#/start" title="Back to Start">
            <span class="brand-mark" aria-hidden="true"></span>RuleForge
          </a>
          <div class="rulebar" id="rulebar" aria-label="The rule being edited"></div>
          <div class="topbar-right">
            <button class="btn ghost sm" id="jump" type="button">
              Jump&hellip; <span class="kbd">Ctrl K</span>
            </button>
            <button class="btn primary sm" id="save-version" type="button">Save version</button>
          </div>
        </header>
      
        <nav class="rail" id="rail" aria-label="Screens"></nav>
      
        <main class="stage">
          <div class="steps" id="steps" aria-label="Authoring steps" hidden></div>
          <div class="stage-scroll" id="screen"></div>
        </main>
      
        <section class="problems is-collapsed" id="problems" data-empty="true"
                 aria-label="Problems" aria-live="polite"></section>
      
        <footer class="statusbar" id="statusbar" aria-label="Status"></footer>
      
      </div>
      
      <div class="toast" id="toast" hidden role="status"></div>
      
      <div class="palette" id="palette" hidden>
        <div class="palette-box">
          <input class="palette-input" type="text" aria-label="Jump to a screen"
                 placeholder="Jump to a screen, or type an action&hellip;" spellcheck="false">
          <div class="palette-list" role="listbox"></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      
      <div class="inspector" id="inspector" hidden></div>
      
      <noscript>
        <p style="padding: 24px; font-family: sans-serif">
          RuleForge needs JavaScript. Nothing is hidden from you, but every screen is
          built in the browser from one state object, so there is no static version.
        </p>
      </noscript>
      
      <script type="module" src="/static/js/main.js"></script>
      </body>
      </html>
      
- path: web\static\js\ui\shell.js
  content: |
      /* The frame around every screen: rail, step rail, rule bar, Problems panel,
         status bar, the jump palette and the state inspector. */
      
      import { h, fmtTime } from './dom.js';
      import { btn, badge } from './components.js';
      import { state, act } from '../core/state.js';
      import { SCREENS, GROUPS, byName, parse, go } from '../core/router.js';
      import { applyFix, dismissProblem } from '../core/problems.js';
      
      let route = parse(window.location.hash);
      
      /* -- rail ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      function railLink(screen, current) {
        const isCurrent = current.name === screen.name ||
          (screen.name === 'versions' && current.name === 'versions');
        const link = h('button', {
          class: 'rail-link' + (isCurrent ? ' is-active' : ''),
          type: 'button',
          title: screen.label,
          on: { click: () => go(screen.name) },
        },
          screen.step
            ? h('span', { class: 'rail-num', text: String(screen.step) })
            : h('span', { class: 'rail-num', text: '\u00b7' }),
          h('span', { class: 'link-text-long', text: screen.label }),
          countFor(screen.name) !== null
            ? h('span', { class: 'rail-count', text: String(countFor(screen.name)) })
            : null);
        return link;
      }
      
      function countFor(name) {
        if (name === 'datasets') return state.cache.datasets.length || null;
        if (name === 'receipts') return state.cache.runs.length || null;
        if (name === 'versions') return state.cache.versions.length || null;
        return null;
      }
      
      export function refreshRail() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#rail');
        if (!host) return;
        host.textContent = '';
        for (const group of GROUPS) {
          const screens = SCREENS.filter((s) => s.group === group);
          const box = h('div', { class: 'rail-group' },
            h('div', { class: 'rail-label', text: group }));
          for (const screen of screens) box.appendChild(railLink(screen, route));
          host.appendChild(box);
        }
        host.appendChild(h('div', { class: 'rail-foot' },
          h('div', {}, 'RuleForge \u00b7 local only'),
          h('div', {}, h('a', { href: '/classic', target: '_blank', rel: 'noreferrer', text: 'Open the old UI' })),
          h('div', { class: 'mono', text: 'Ctrl+K to jump' })));
      }
      
      /* -- steps ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      export function refreshSteps() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#steps');
        if (!host) return;
        const ruleScreens = SCREENS.filter((s) => s.step);
        const onRule = ruleScreens.some((s) => s.name === route.name);
        host.hidden = !onRule;
        if (!onRule) { host.textContent = ''; return; }
        host.textContent = '';
        const currentStep = byName(route.name).step || 0;
        for (const screen of ruleScreens) {
          const isDone = screen.step < currentStep;
          host.appendChild(h('button', {
            class: 'step' + (screen.name === route.name ? ' is-current' : '') +
              (isDone ? ' is-done' : ''),
            type: 'button',
            on: { click: () => go(screen.name) },
          },
            h('span', { class: 'step-num', text: String(screen.step) }),
            screen.label));
          if (screen.step < ruleScreens.length) {
            host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'step-arrow', text: '\u203a' }));
          }
        }
      }
      
      /* -- rule bar ------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      export function refreshRuleBar() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#rulebar');
        if (!host) return;
        host.textContent = '';
        const rule = state.doc.payload && state.doc.payload.rule;
        const title = rule && rule.annotations.title.v;
        const name = title || (rule ? rule.rule_id.v : 'untitled');
        const filters = rule
          ? rule.pipeline.v.filter((s) => s['@'] === 'Filter').length : 0;
      
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'rulebar-title', text: name, title: name }));
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'rulebar-sep', text: '\u00b7' }));
        /* One rule, one identity: repeating the id because the title is empty read
           as two different rules side by side. */
        const parts = [];
        if (title && rule && title !== rule.rule_id.v) parts.push(rule.rule_id.v);
        parts.push(filters + (filters === 1 ? ' condition' : ' conditions'));
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'rulebar-meta', text: parts.join(' \u00b7 ') }));
        if (state.ui.dirty) {
          host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'dirty-dot', title: 'unsaved changes' }));
          host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'rulebar-meta', text: 'unsaved' }));
        }
      }
      
      /* -- problems ------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      const SEVERITY_ORDER = { error: 0, warning: 1, caution: 2, info: 3 };
      
      export function refreshProblems() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#problems');
        if (!host) return;
        const problems = state.ui.problems.slice().sort(
          (a, b) => (SEVERITY_ORDER[a.severity] ?? 9) - (SEVERITY_ORDER[b.severity] ?? 9),
        );
        host.dataset.empty = problems.length ? 'false' : 'true';
        host.textContent = '';
        if (!problems.length) return;
      
        const collapsed = host.classList.contains('is-collapsed');
        host.appendChild(h('div', { class: 'problems-head' },
          h('span', {
            class: 'badge ' + (problems.some((p) => p.severity === 'error') ? 'danger' : 'caution'),
            text: problems.length + (problems.length === 1 ? ' problem' : ' problems'),
          }),
          h('span', { class: 'grow muted', text: collapsed ? 'hidden \u2014 show to read them' : '' }),
          btn(collapsed ? 'Show' : 'Hide', {
            size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet',
            onClick: () => {
              host.classList.toggle('is-collapsed');
              refreshProblems();
            },
          })));
      
        const body = h('div', { class: 'problems-body' });
        for (const problem of problems) {
          body.appendChild(h('div', { class: 'problem' },
            h('span', { class: 'problem-code', text: problem.code }),
            h('div', {},
              h('div', { class: 'problem-plain', text: problem.plain }),
              problem.message && problem.message !== problem.plain
                ? h('div', { class: 'problem-engine', text: problem.message })
                : null),
            h('div', { class: 'problem-fix row' },
              problem.fix
                ? btn(problem.fix.label + ' \u2192', {
                  size: 'sm',
                  onClick: () => applyFix(problem.fix),
                })
                : null,
              btn('\u00d7', {
                size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', title: 'dismiss',
                onClick: () => dismissProblem(problem.code),
              }))));
        }
        host.appendChild(body);
      }
      
      /* -- status bar ----------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      export function refreshStatusBar() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#statusbar');
        if (!host) return;
        host.textContent = '';
      
        const dialect = state.cache.dialects.find((d) => d.key === state.ui.target);
        const health = state.status.health;
        const healthState = health === null ? '' : (health ? ' dot--ok' : ' dot--bad');
        const verdict = state.status.lastVerdict;
      
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'status-item' },
          h('span', { class: 'dot' + healthState }),
          h('b', { text: health === null ? 'checking' : (health ? 'server ok' : 'server down') })));
      
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'status-item' },
          h('b', { text: 'target' }), dialect ? dialect.label : state.ui.target));
      
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'status-item' },
          h('b', { text: 'rule' }),
          state.status.ruleHash ? String(state.status.ruleHash).slice(0, 8) : 'unsaved'));
      
        if (state.status.datasetHash) {
          host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'status-item' },
            h('b', { text: 'dataset' }), String(state.status.datasetHash).slice(0, 8)));
        }
      
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'status-item' },
          h('b', { text: 'verdict' }),
          state.status.staleVerdict ? 'stale (sample changed)'
            : verdict === null ? 'not run'
              : ({ matched: 'matched', no_match: 'no match', not_evaluated: 'could not tell' }[verdict] || verdict)));
      
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'status-spacer' }));
      
        if (state.draftSavedAt) {
          host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'status-item' },
            h('b', { text: 'draft' }), fmtTime(state.draftSavedAt)));
        }
        host.appendChild(h('span', { class: 'status-item' },
          h('span', { class: 'dot' + (state.ui.busy ? ' dot--caution' : '') }),
          state.ui.busy ? 'working' : 'idle'));
      }
      
      /** The parts that follow an edit: the rule bar and the status bar. The rail
          does not change while typing, and rebuilding it on every keystroke is
          wasted work that can steal focus. */
      export function refreshEditing() {
        refreshRuleBar();
        refreshStatusBar();
      }
      
      export function refreshShell(nextRoute) {
        if (nextRoute) route = nextRoute;
        else route = parse(window.location.hash);
        refreshRail();
        refreshSteps();
        refreshRuleBar();
        refreshProblems();
        refreshStatusBar();
      }
      
      /* -- jump palette --------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      let paletteIndex = 0;
      let paletteResults = [];
      
      function paletteEntries(query) {
        const needle = String(query || '').toLowerCase();
        const entries = SCREENS.map((screen) => ({
          label: screen.label,
          group: screen.group,
          href: screen.name,
        }));
        entries.push(
          { label: 'Save version', group: 'ACTION', href: 'action:save' },
          { label: 'Run the health check', group: 'ACTION', href: 'health' },
          { label: 'Open the state inspector', group: 'ACTION', href: 'action:inspect' },
        );
        return entries.filter((entry) =>
          !needle || (entry.label + ' ' + entry.group).toLowerCase().includes(needle));
      }
      
      function renderPalette() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#palette');
        if (!host || host.hidden) return;
        const list = host.querySelector('.palette-list');
        list.textContent = '';
        paletteResults.forEach((entry, index) => {
          list.appendChild(h('button', {
            class: 'palette-item' + (index === paletteIndex ? ' is-active' : ''),
            type: 'button',
            on: {
              click: () => {
                closePalette();
                if (entry.href === 'action:save') {
                  document.querySelector('#save-version').click();
                } else if (entry.href === 'action:inspect') {
                  openInspector();
                } else {
                  go(entry.href);
                }
              },
            },
          }, entry.label, h('span', { class: 'palette-group', text: entry.group })));
        });
        if (!paletteResults.length) {
          list.appendChild(h('div', { class: 'palette-item', text: 'No screen matches that.' }));
        }
      }
      
      export function openPalette() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#palette');
        if (!host) return;
        host.hidden = false;
        const search = host.querySelector('.palette-input');
        search.value = '';
        paletteIndex = 0;
        paletteResults = paletteEntries('');
        renderPalette();
        search.focus();
      }
      
      export function closePalette() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#palette');
        if (host) host.hidden = true;
      }
      
      /* -- inspector ------------------------------------------------------------ */
      
      export function openInspector() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#inspector');
        if (!host) return;
        host.hidden = false;
        host.textContent = '';
        const box = h('div', { class: 'inspector-box' },
          h('header', {},
            h('span', { class: 'eyebrow grow', text: 'State inspector' }),
            btn('Close', { size: 'sm', kind: 'quiet', onClick: closeInspector })),
          h('div', { class: 'inspector-body' },
            h('div', {},
              h('h3', { text: 'UI state' }),
              h('pre', { text: JSON.stringify({
                screen: state.ui.screen,
                target: state.ui.target,
                dirty: state.ui.dirty,
                problems: state.ui.problems.map((p) => p.code),
                draftsSavedAt: state.draftSavedAt,
              }, null, 2) })),
            h('div', {},
              h('h3', { text: 'The rule payload (what every request sends)' }),
              h('pre', { text: JSON.stringify(state.doc.payload, null, 2) })),
            h('div', {},
              h('h3', { text: 'Last request' }),
              h('pre', { text: JSON.stringify(state.ui.lastRequest, null, 2) })),
            h('div', {},
              h('h3', { text: 'Last response' }),
              h('pre', { text: JSON.stringify(state.ui.lastResponse, null, 2) }))));
        box.onclick = (event) => event.stopPropagation();
        host.appendChild(box);
        host.onclick = closeInspector;
      }
      
      export function closeInspector() {
        const host = document.querySelector('#inspector');
        if (host) host.hidden = true;
      }
      
      /* -- boot ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      export function bindShell(options) {
        const opts = options || {};
      
        document.querySelector('#save-version').onclick = () => opts.onSaveVersion();
        document.querySelector('#jump').onclick = openPalette;
      
        document.querySelector('#palette').onclick = (event) => {
          if (event.target.id === 'palette') closePalette();
        };
        const search = document.querySelector('#palette .palette-input');
        search.addEventListener('input', () => {
          paletteIndex = 0;
          paletteResults = paletteEntries(search.value);
          renderPalette();
        });
        search.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
          if (event.key === 'Escape') { closePalette(); return; }
          if (event.key === 'ArrowDown') {
            event.preventDefault();
            paletteIndex = Math.min(paletteIndex + 1, paletteResults.length - 1);
            renderPalette();
          } else if (event.key === 'ArrowUp') {
            event.preventDefault();
            paletteIndex = Math.max(paletteIndex - 1, 0);
            renderPalette();
          } else if (event.key === 'Enter') {
            const entry = paletteResults[paletteIndex];
            if (!entry) return;
            closePalette();
            if (entry.href === 'action:save') document.querySelector('#save-version').click();
            else if (entry.href === 'action:inspect') openInspector();
            else go(entry.href);
          }
        });
      
        document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
          const mod = event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey;
          if (mod && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'k') {
            event.preventDefault();
            if (document.querySelector('#palette').hidden) openPalette();
            else closePalette();
            return;
          }
          if (mod && event.shiftKey && event.key.toLowerCase() === 'd') {
            event.preventDefault();
            openInspector();
            return;
          }
          if (mod && event.key.toLowerCase() === 's') {
            event.preventDefault();
            opts.onSaveVersion();
            return;
          }
          if (event.key === 'Escape') {
            closePalette();
            closeInspector();
          }
        });
      
        /* The health dot is only honest if it is recent. */
        const ping = () => opts.onPing();
        ping();
        setInterval(ping, 20000);
      
        refreshShell();
        act(() => {});
      }
      
- path: web\static\js\core\router.js
  content: |
      /* Hash router. Every screen is a URL, so a bug can be linked, reloaded and
         reproduced — the old UI had no addressable state at all. */
      
      export const SCREENS = [
        { name: 'start', group: 'AUTHOR', label: 'Start', href: '#/start' },
        { name: 'details', group: 'AUTHOR', label: 'Details', step: 1, href: '#/rule/draft/details' },
        { name: 'source', group: 'AUTHOR', label: 'Source', step: 2, href: '#/rule/draft/source' },
        { name: 'conditions', group: 'AUTHOR', label: 'Conditions', step: 3, href: '#/rule/draft/conditions' },
        { name: 'stages', group: 'AUTHOR', label: 'Stage library', step: 4, href: '#/rule/draft/stages' },
        { name: 'preview', group: 'AUTHOR', label: 'Preview', step: 5, href: '#/rule/draft/preview' },
        { name: 'test', group: 'VERIFY', label: 'Test', step: 6, href: '#/rule/draft/test' },
        { name: 'datasets', group: 'VERIFY', label: 'Datasets', href: '#/datasets' },
        { name: 'receipts', group: 'VERIFY', label: 'Receipts', href: '#/receipts' },
        { name: 'versions', group: 'VERIFY', label: 'Versions', href: '#/versions' },
        { name: 'explain', group: 'DERIVE', label: 'Explain a rule', href: '#/explain' },
        { name: 'draft', group: 'DERIVE', label: 'Draft from logs', href: '#/draft' },
        { name: 'reference', group: 'REF', label: 'Reference', href: '#/reference' },
        { name: 'health', group: 'REF', label: 'Health', href: '#/health' },
      ];
      
      export const GROUPS = ['AUTHOR', 'VERIFY', 'DERIVE', 'REF'];
      
      const RULE_SCREENS = new Set(
        ['details', 'source', 'conditions', 'stages', 'preview', 'test'],
      );
      
      export function byName(name) {
        return SCREENS.find((s) => s.name === name) || SCREENS[0];
      }
      
      export function parse(hash) {
        const raw = String(hash || '').replace(/^#/, '');
        const [pathPart, queryPart] = raw.split('?');
        const path = pathPart.split('/').filter(Boolean);
        const query = new URLSearchParams(queryPart || '');
      
        if (!path.length) return { name: 'start', query };
      
        if (path[0] === 'rule') {
          const ruleId = path[1] || 'draft';
          const name = RULE_SCREENS.has(path[2]) ? path[2] : 'details';
          return { name, ruleId, query };
        }
        if (path[0] === 'datasets') return { name: 'datasets', id: path[1] || null, query };
        if (path[0] === 'receipts') return { name: 'receipts', id: path[1] || null, query };
        if (path[0] === 'versions') return { name: 'versions', id: path[1] || null, query };
        if (path[0] === 'reference') return { name: 'reference', code: path[1] || null, query };
        if (path[0] === 'explain') return { name: 'explain', query };
        if (path[0] === 'draft') return { name: 'draft', query };
        if (path[0] === 'health') return { name: 'health', query };
        return { name: 'start', query };
      }
      
      /** The URL for a screen, keeping the current rule id when the screen is a rule
          screen. `draft` is replaced by the stored id only after a save. */
      export function href(name, options) {
        const opts = options || {};
        if (name === 'start') return '#/start';
        if (RULE_SCREENS.has(name)) {
          return '#/rule/' + (opts.ruleId || 'draft') + '/' + name;
        }
        if (name === 'datasets' || name === 'receipts' || name === 'versions') {
          return '#/' + name + (opts.id ? '/' + opts.id : '');
        }
        if (name === 'reference' && opts.code) return '#/reference/' + opts.code;
        return '#/' + name;
      }
      
      export function go(name, options) {
        const next = href(name, options);
        if (window.location.hash === next) {
          window.dispatchEvent(new HashChangeEvent('hashchange'));
          return;
        }
        window.location.hash = next;
      }
      
      export const nextStepOf = (name) => {
        const index = SCREENS.findIndex((s) => s.name === name);
        if (index < 0) return null;
        const next = SCREENS[index + 1];
        return next && next.step ? next : null;
      };
      
      export const previousStepOf = (name) => {
        const index = SCREENS.findIndex((s) => s.name === name);
        if (index <= 0) return null;
        const previous = SCREENS[index - 1];
        return previous && previous.step ? previous : null;
      };
      
- path: web\static\js\screens\shared.js
  content: |
      /* Small helpers shared by the rule screens. */
      
      import { h } from '../ui/dom.js';
      import { btn } from '../ui/components.js';
      import { state, doc, mutate, touch, stages } from '../core/state.js';
      import { go, nextStepOf } from '../core/router.js';
      import { T, linesOf } from '../core/ir.js';
      
      export const annotations = () => doc().annotations;
      
      export const readStage = () => stages().find((s) => s['@'] === 'Read') || null;
      
      export function page(title, options) {
        const opts = options || {};
        return h('div', { class: 'page' },
          h('div', { class: 'page-head' },
            h('div', { class: 'grow' },
              h('span', { class: 'eyebrow', text: opts.eyebrow || '' }),
              h('h1', { text: title }),
              opts.sub ? h('p', { class: 'page-sub', text: opts.sub }) : null),
            opts.actions ? h('div', { class: 'btn-row' }, opts.actions) : null),
          opts.body || null);
      }
      
      /** The visible order of the authoring screens, with one way forward. */
      export function nextStepFooter(current) {
        const next = nextStepOf(current);
        if (!next) return null;
        return h('div', { class: 'next-step' },
          h('span', { class: 'muted', text: 'The screen after this one is ' + next.label + '.' }),
          btn('Next: ' + next.label + ' \u2192', {
            kind: 'primary',
            onClick: () => go(next.name),
          }));
      }
      
      /** Bind a text input to a tagged IR field, without losing the caret. */
      export function boundText(options) {
        const opts = options || {};
        return h('input', {
          class: 'input' + (opts.code ? ' code' : ''),
          id: opts.id || null,
          type: opts.type || 'text',
          value: opts.value || '',
          placeholder: opts.placeholder || null,
          spellcheck: false,
          autocomplete: 'off',
          on: {
            input: () => {
              const node = document.getElementById(opts.id);
              mutate(() => { opts.commit(node ? node.value : ''); });
              if (opts.afterInput) opts.afterInput();
            },
            change: opts.onChange,
          },
        });
      }
      
      export function boundTextarea(options) {
        const opts = options || {};
        return h('textarea', {
          class: 'textarea' + (opts.code ? ' code' : ''),
          id: opts.id || null,
          rows: opts.rows || 4,
          placeholder: opts.placeholder || null,
          spellcheck: false,
          value: opts.value || '',
          on: {
            input: () => {
              const node = document.getElementById(opts.id);
              mutate(() => { opts.commit(node ? node.value : ''); });
            },
          },
        });
      }
      
      /* -- annotation helpers --------------------------------------------------- */
      
      export const mitreToText = () => annotations().mitre_attack.v.map((pair) => {
        const tactic = pair.v[0].v;
        const techniques = pair.v[1].v.map((t) => t.v).join(', ');
        return techniques ? tactic + ': ' + techniques : tactic;
      }).join('\n');
      
      export const mitreFromText = (text) => linesOf(text).map((line) => {
        const colon = line.indexOf(':');
        const tactic = colon < 0 ? line.trim() : line.slice(0, colon).trim();
        const techniques = colon < 0 ? []
          : line.slice(colon + 1).split(',').map((t) => t.trim()).filter(Boolean);
        return T.tuple([T.str(tactic), T.tuple(techniques.map(T.str))]);
      });
      
      export const listText = (tuple) => tuple.v.map((item) => item.v).join('\n');
      export const listFromText = (text) => T.tuple(linesOf(text).map(T.str));
      
      export const severityOptions = [
        { value: '', label: '\u2014' },
        { value: 'informational', label: 'informational' },
        { value: 'low', label: 'low' },
        { value: 'medium', label: 'medium' },
        { value: 'high', label: 'high' },
        { value: 'critical', label: 'critical' },
      ];
      
      /** Set the id used in the URL once the rule is saved. */
      export function noteRuleId(value) {
        state.doc.ruleId = value || 'draft';
      }
      
      export { touch };
      
- path: web\static\js\main.js
  content: |
      /* Entry point: build the shell, restore the draft, route. */
      
      import { state, setRenderer, restoreDraft, rerender, onChrome } from './core/state.js';
      import { parse, byName } from './core/router.js';
      import { attempt, setNotifier, problemFromError } from './core/problems.js';
      import { toast } from './ui/components.js';
      import { bindShell, refreshShell, refreshEditing } from './ui/shell.js';
      import { mount } from './ui/dom.js';
      import * as api from './core/api.js';
      import { saveVersionNow } from './screens/versions.js';
      
      import * as start from './screens/start.js';
      import * as details from './screens/details.js';
      import * as source from './screens/source.js';
      import * as conditions from './screens/conditions.js';
      import * as stages from './screens/stages.js';
      import * as preview from './screens/preview.js';
      import * as test from './screens/test.js';
      import * as datasets from './screens/datasets.js';
      import * as receipts from './screens/receipts.js';
      import * as versions from './screens/versions.js';
      import * as explain from './screens/explain.js';
      import * as draft from './screens/draft.js';
      import * as reference from './screens/reference.js';
      import * as health from './screens/health.js';
      
      const SCREENS = {
        start, details, source, conditions, stages, preview, test,
        datasets, receipts, versions, explain, draft, reference, health,
      };
      
      let lastHash = null;
      
      function render() {
        const hash = window.location.hash || '#/start';
        const fresh = hash !== lastHash;
        lastHash = hash;
        const route = parse(hash);
        const screen = SCREENS[route.name] || SCREENS.start;
        state.ui.screen = route.name;
      
        const host = document.getElementById('screen');
        try {
          mount(host, screen.render(route, fresh));
          host.scrollTop = 0;
        } catch (err) {
          /* A screen that throws must not leave a blank page with no explanation. */
          const problem = problemFromError(err, route.name);
          problem.plain = 'The ' + byName(route.name).label + ' screen failed to ' +
            'build: ' + (err && err.message ? err.message : String(err));
          problem.fix = null;
          state.ui.problems.push(problem);
          mount(host, null);
          toast(problem.plain, 'bad', problem.code);
        }
      
        refreshShell(route);
        document.title = byName(route.name).label + ' \u00b7 RuleForge';
      }
      
      setRenderer(render);
      setNotifier((problem) => {
        toast(problem.plain, 'bad', problem.code);
      });
      
      window.addEventListener('hashchange', () => {
        render();
      });
      
      window.addEventListener('error', (event) => {
        const problem = problemFromError(event.error || event.message, 'page');
        problem.plain = 'An uncaught error stopped part of the page: ' +
          (event.message || 'unknown');
        state.ui.problems.push(problem);
        refreshShell();
      });
      
      window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', (event) => {
        const problem = problemFromError(event.reason, 'page');
        state.ui.problems.push(problem);
        toast(problem.plain, 'bad', problem.code);
        refreshShell();
      });
      
      /* The status bar's health dot must reflect a real answer, and only a real
         answer. `onPing` is called on boot and every 20 seconds. */
      async function ping() {
        try {
          const data = await api.health();
          state.status.health = !!data.ok;
        } catch (err) {
          state.status.health = false;
        }
        refreshShell();
      }
      
      function boot() {
        restoreDraft();
        bindShell({
          onSaveVersion: () => saveVersionNow(),
          onPing: () => ping(),
        });
        if (!window.location.hash) window.location.hash = '#/start';
        render();
      
        attempt(async () => {
          const data = await api.dialects();
          state.cache.dialects = data.dialects || [];
          const ready = state.cache.dialects.find((d) => d.status === 'ready');
          if (ready && !state.cache.dialects.some((d) => d.key === state.ui.target)) {
            state.ui.target = ready.key;
          }
          rerender();
        }, { context: 'boot' });
      
        /* The rail shows how much evidence exists, so the counts are fetched once at
           start rather than on every navigation. */
        attempt(async () => {
          const [datasets, runs, versions] = await Promise.all([
            api.datasets(''),
            api.testRuns(),
            api.history({ limit: 100 }),
          ]);
          state.cache.datasets = datasets.datasets || [];
          state.cache.runs = runs.test_runs || [];
          state.cache.versions = versions.entries || [];
          refreshShell();
        }, { context: 'boot' });
      
        onChrome(() => {
          /* The rule bar and status bar follow every edit without redrawing the
             screen, so typing never loses the caret. */
          refreshEditing();
        });
      }
      
      boot();

  content: |
      /* 5 Preview — the rule in another language.
      
         The pane names the language next to the text, and a render that is older
         than the rule says so in words. The old UI let the label contradict the
         content, which is how KQL got copied into a Splunk deployment. */
      
      import { h } from '../ui/dom.js';
      import { badge, btn, card, codeBlock, toast } from '../ui/components.js';
      import { state, rerender } from '../core/state.js';
      import { attempt } from '../core/problems.js';
      import { nextStepFooter, page } from './shared.js';
      import * as api from '../core/api.js';
      
      let last = { text: '', target: null, edits: -1, diagnostics: [] };
      
      export function render(route, fresh) {
        /* Re-render on arrival: the rule may have changed on another screen, and a
           stale pane that looks authoritative is the one failure this tool must
           never have. */
        if (fresh) doRender();
      
        const stale = last.edits !== state.ui.edits;
        const diagnostics = last.diagnostics || [];
      
        const dialectList = h('div', { class: 'dialect-list' },
          ...state.cache.dialects.map((dialect) => h('button', {
            class: 'dialect-item' + (dialect.key === state.ui.target ? ' is-active' : ''),
            type: 'button',
            disabled: dialect.status !== 'ready',
            title: dialect.note || (dialect.status === 'ready'
              ? 'render into ' + dialect.label
              : 'not implemented yet'),
            on: { click: () => setTarget(dialect.key) },
          },
            h('span', { class: 'muted mono', text: dialect.status === 'ready' ? '\u25cf' : '\u25cb' }),
            h('span', {},
              h('span', { class: 'dialect-label', text: dialect.label }),
              h('span', { class: 'dialect-sub', text: dialect.language +
                (dialect.status === 'ready' ? '' : ' \u00b7 planned') })),
            dialect.carries_annotations
              ? badge('annotations', 'ok', 'this language carries the title, severity and ATT&CK mapping')
              : badge('query only', null, 'this language cannot carry title, severity or ATT&CK mapping'))));
      
        const pane = h('div', { class: 'stack' });
        if (stale && last.text) {
          pane.appendChild(h('div', { class: 'stale-note', text:
            'The rule has changed since this text was rendered. Press Render to see ' +
            'the rule as it is now \u2014 this is the PREVIOUS output.' }));
        }
        pane.appendChild(codeBlock({
          text: last.text || '\u2014',
          id: 'rendered',
          labelId: 'rendered-for',
          label: targetName(state.ui.target) + (last.target && last.target !== state.ui.target
            ? ' \u00b7 showing the previous target' : ''),
          copy: !!last.text,
        }));
      
        if (diagnostics.length) {
          const notes = h('div', { class: 'stack' });
          for (const note of diagnostics) {
            notes.appendChild(h('div', {
              class: 'problem',
              style: { gridTemplateColumns: '92px minmax(0, 1fr)' },
            },
              h('span', { class: 'problem-code', text: note.code }),
              h('div', {},
                h('div', { class: 'problem-plain', text: note.message }),
                note.where ? h('div', { class: 'problem-engine', text: note.where }) : null,
                note.verified === false
                  ? h('div', { class: 'problem-engine', text:
                    'inferred from the rule, not measured against a sample' })
                  : null)));
          }
          pane.appendChild(h('div', { id: 'diagnostics' }, card({
            title: diagnostics.length + ' thing(s) the target language does not say',
            sub: 'This text is not wrong; it is narrower or broader than the rule. ' +
              'Read these before deploying it.',
            body: notes,
          })));
        } else {
          pane.appendChild(h('div', { id: 'diagnostics' }));
        }
      
        const actions = h('div', { class: 'btn-row' },
          btn('Render', { kind: 'primary', id: 'render', onClick: doRender }),
          btn('Validate', { id: 'validate', onClick: doValidate }),
          btn('Copy', {
            onClick: async () => {
              try {
                await navigator.clipboard.writeText(last.text);
                toast('Copied the rendered rule.', 'good');
              } catch (err) {
                toast('The browser refused clipboard access; select the text instead.', 'bad');
              }
            },
          }));
      
        return page('Preview', {
          eyebrow: 'Step 5 of 6 \u00b7 author',
          sub: 'The same rule, written in the language a particular SIEM accepts. ' +
            'Change the target on the left; the text changes, the rule does not.',
          actions,
          body: h('div', { class: 'stack-lg' },
            h('div', { class: 'author-col' },
              card({
                title: 'Target language',
                sub: state.cache.dialects.filter((d) => d.status === 'ready').length +
                  ' of ' + state.cache.dialects.length + ' are implemented.',
                body: dialectList,
              }),
              h('div', { class: 'stack' }, pane, refusalNote())),
            nextStepFooter('preview'))});
      }
      
      function refusalNote() {
        return card({
          title: 'What a refusal means',
          body: h('div', { class: 'stack' },
            h('p', { class: 'dim' },
              'When the rule cannot be expressed in the target language, this pane ' +
              'is emptied and the reason is shown. It is never a best-effort ' +
              'translation: a rule that quietly matches more than you meant is ' +
              'worse than no rule at all.'),
            h('p', { class: 'dim' },
              'Validate lints the rule itself — including a screen for patterns ' +
              'that would hang the engine that runs it.')),
        });
      }
      
      function targetName(key) {
        const found = state.cache.dialects.find((d) => d.key === key);
        return found ? found.label + ' (' + found.language + ')' : key;
      }
      
      function setTarget(key) {
        if (key === state.ui.target) return;
        state.ui.target = key;
        rerender();
        doRender();
      }
      
      export function doRender() {
        const target = state.ui.target;
        const edits = state.ui.edits;
        attempt(async () => {
          const data = await api.render(target, state.doc.payload);
          /* If the target changed while this was in flight, showing the answer to
             the old question under the new label is the lie this screen exists to
             prevent. */
          if (target !== state.ui.target) return;
          last = {
            text: data.text,
            target,
            edits,
            diagnostics: data.diagnostics || [],
          };
          rerender();
        }, { context: 'preview' });
      }
      
      function doValidate() {
        attempt(async () => {
          const data = await api.validate(state.doc.payload);
          toast('The rule is structurally sound and no pattern in it would hang the ' +
            'engine that runs it.', 'good');
          if (data.outline) {
            state.cache.lastOutline = data.outline;
          }
        }, { context: 'preview' });
      }

  content: |
      /* The application frame and every reusable component. */
      
      /* -- frame ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      .app {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: var(--rail-width) minmax(0, 1fr);
        grid-template-rows: var(--topbar-height) minmax(0, 1fr) auto var(--statusbar-height);
        grid-template-areas:
          "topbar topbar"
          "rail stage"
          "problems problems"
          "status status";
        height: 100vh;
        overflow: hidden;
      }
      
      .topbar {
        grid-area: topbar;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: var(--space-3);
        padding: 0 var(--space-4);
        background: var(--surface-shell);
        border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-quiet);
      }
      
      .brand {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 8px;
        font-size: 14px;
        font-weight: 700;
        letter-spacing: -0.02em;
        color: var(--text-primary);
        text-decoration: none;
        padding-right: var(--space-3);
        border-right: 1px solid var(--border-quiet);
        height: 28px;
      }
      
      .brand:hover {
        text-decoration: none;
      }
      
      .brand span {
        color: var(--accent);
      }
      
      .brand-mark {
        width: 8px;
        height: 8px;
        border-radius: 2px;
        background: var(--accent);
        box-shadow: 0 0 12px var(--accent);
      }
      
      .rulebar {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: var(--space-2);
        min-width: 0;
        flex: 1 1 auto;
        font-size: 12px;
        color: var(--text-secondary);
      }
      
      .rulebar-title {
        font-weight: 600;
        color: var(--text-primary);
        max-width: 34ch;
        overflow: hidden;
        text-overflow: ellipsis;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      
      .rulebar-sep {
        color: var(--text-muted);
      }
      
      .rulebar-meta {
        color: var(--text-muted);
        font-family: var(--font-mono);
        font-size: 11px;
        white-space: nowrap;
        overflow: hidden;
        text-overflow: ellipsis;
      }
      
      .topbar-right {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: var(--space-2);
        margin-left: auto;
      }
      
      .dirty-dot {
        width: 7px;
        height: 7px;
        border-radius: 50%;
        background: var(--state-caution);
        box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--state-caution);
      }
      
      /* -- rail ----------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      .rail {
        grid-area: rail;
        background: var(--surface-rail);
        border-right: 1px solid var(--border-quiet);
        overflow-y: auto;
        padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-2) var(--space-5);
      }
      
      .rail-group + .rail-group {
        margin-top: var(--space-4);
      }
      
      .rail-label {
        padding: var(--space-1) var(--space-2);
        font-size: 9px;
        font-weight: 700;
        letter-spacing: 0.14em;
        color: var(--text-muted);
      }
      
      .rail-link {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: var(--space-2);
        width: 100%;
        padding: 7px var(--space-2);
        border: 0;
        border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
        background: transparent;
        color: var(--text-secondary);
        font-size: 12.5px;
        text-align: left;
        cursor: pointer;
        transition: background var(--fast), color var(--fast);
      }
      
      .rail-link:hover {
        background: var(--surface-hover);
        color: var(--text-primary);
      }
      
      .rail-link.is-active {
        background: var(--surface-active);
        color: var(--text-primary);
        box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--accent);
      }
      
      .rail-num {
        display: inline-flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        width: 18px;
        height: 18px;
        border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
        background: var(--surface-raised);
        color: var(--text-muted);
        font-family: var(--font-mono);
        font-size: 10px;
        flex: 0 0 auto;
      }
      
      .rail-link.is-active .rail-num {
        background: var(--accent-soft);
        color: var(--accent-strong);
      }
      
      .rail-count {
        margin-left: auto;
        font-family: var(--font-mono);
        font-size: 10px;
        color: var(--text-muted);
      }
      
      .rail-foot {
        margin-top: var(--space-5);
        padding: var(--space-2);
        border-top: 1px solid var(--border-quiet);
        font-size: 11px;
        color: var(--text-muted);
        line-height: 1.7;
      }
      
      .rail-foot a {
        color: var(--text-secondary);
      }
      
      /* -- stage ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      .stage {
        grid-area: stage;
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        min-height: 0;
        background: var(--surface-page);
      }
      
      .steps {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: var(--space-1);
        padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-4);
        border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-quiet);
        background: var(--surface-shell);
        overflow-x: auto;
      }
      
      .steps[hidden] {
        display: none;
      }
      
      .step {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 6px;
        padding: 5px 10px;
        border: 1px solid transparent;
        border-radius: var(--radius-pill);
        background: transparent;
        color: var(--text-muted);
        font-size: 11.5px;
        white-space: nowrap;
        cursor: pointer;
      }
      
      .step:hover {
        color: var(--text-primary);
        background: var(--surface-hover);
      }
      
      .step.is-done {
        color: var(--text-secondary);
      }
      
      .step.is-done .step-num {
        border-color: var(--state-ok);
        color: var(--state-ok);
      }
      
      .step.is-current {
        border-color: var(--border-strong);
        background: var(--surface-card);
        color: var(--text-primary);
      }
      
      .step.is-current .step-num {
        background: var(--accent);
        border-color: var(--accent);
        color: var(--text-inverse);
      }
      
      .step-num {
        display: inline-flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        width: 16px;
        height: 16px;
        border: 1px solid var(--border-strong);
        border-radius: 50%;
        font-family: var(--font-mono);
        font-size: 9px;
      }
      
      .step-arrow {
        color: var(--border-strong);
        font-size: 11px;
      }
      
      .stage-scroll {
        flex: 1 1 auto;
        min-height: 0;
        overflow-y: auto;
      }
      
      /* -- problems ------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      .problems {
        grid-area: problems;
        border-top: 1px solid var(--border-quiet);
        background: var(--surface-shell);
        max-height: 42vh;

        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: var(--space-2);
        padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-4);
        font-size: 11.5px;

> _Reasoning_
> Now I understand the structure. Time to write. Plan the new architecture:
>

> - `#/studio/{datasets,receipts,history,explain,draft,reference,health}` (+ optional id)
> 
> **SCREENS array** (for palette + labels), all with `view`:

> { name:'home', label:'Home', href:'#/' }

> { name:'datasets' }, {name:'receipts'}, {name:'versions' label:'History'}, {name:'explain'}, {name:'draft'}, {name:'reference'}, {name:'health'}
> ```
> Keep `byName` etc.
> 
> **index.html chrome**
> 
> ```

>     <nav class="mainnav" id="mainnav">

>     <div class="topbar-right">
>       <span class="env" id="env"><span class="dot"></span>Local only</span>
>       <label class="target-pick"><span class="target-label">Target</span>
>         <select id="target"></select></label>
>       <button id="save-version" class="btn primary sm">Save version</button>
>       <button id="jump" class="btn ghost sm icon">⌘K?</button>
>     </div>
>   </header>
>   <nav class="subnav" id="subnav" hidden aria-label="Studio"></nav>
>   <main class="stage">
>     <div class="authorbar" id="authorbar" hidden>
>       <div class="rulebar" id="rulebar"></div>
>       <div class="steps" id="steps"></div>
>     </div>
>     <div class="stage-scroll" id="screen"></div>
>   </main>
>   ...
> </div>
> ```
> 
> Home is a full-bleed page; body should scroll on home. Currently `.app` is 100vh grid with `stage-scroll` overflow. Home content can scroll inside stage-scroll — fine.
> 
> For Home, I want the full-width look with no max-width constraint: `.page.wide` maybe. Home render returns `.home` div; CSS sets its own max-width but hero is wide.
> 
> **Subnav**: rendered by shell from TOOLS; active item from route. Health pushed right with `margin-left:auto`.
> 
> **authorbar**: shows rulebar + steps; visible only when route is an author step.
> 
> **Target select**: topbar. Change → set `state.ui.target`; then `rerender()` (screen rebuild) — but preview's `last` shows stale note since edits unchanged... preview compares last.target !== state.ui.target and labels "showing the previous target", plus `stale` false. On rerender after target change, preview should re-render automatically. I'll subscribe: in shell change handler, set target then `rerender()`; in preview's render, if `last.target !== state.ui.target` and not `fresh`, call `doRender()`? Careful about loops: doRender → rerender → render (fresh false) → if last.target still !== target while in flight → calls doRender again → infinite loop.
> 
> Safer: shell target change dispatches `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('rf:target', {detail:key}))`; preview registers a listener on mount... screens don't have mount hooks. 
> 
> Alternative simpler: keep preview's own dialect list (it's better: shows readiness, annotations capability, status) and make the topbar select call a shared function that changes target and then `go(route)`? Hmm.
> 
> Cleanest minimal: implement a tiny target pub/sub in core/state.js:
> ```js
> const targetWatchers = new Set();
> export function onTargetChange(fn) { targetWatchers.add(fn); return () => targetWatchers.delete(fn); }
> export function setTarget(key) { if (state.ui.target === key) return; state.ui.target = key; for (const fn of targetWatchers) fn(key); }
> ```
> Shell writes via setTarget. Preview subscribes once at module load with a handler that: if current route is preview → `doRender(); rerender()`; else just nothing (its render on arrival calls doRender when fresh). Also update preview's own chips to use setTarget. And `refreshTarget()` to sync the select's value after programmatic changes — subscribe in shell too.
> 
> Careful recursion: setTarget → watchers → preview doRender (async) + rerender; shell target watcher updates select value (no dispatch). Fine.
> 
> **Home page content** (must mirror the screenshot vibe):
> 
> ```
> section.home-hero
>   div.hero-copy
>     eyebrow: LOCAL DETECTION WORKBENCH
>     h1: A workbench for <em>detection rules.</em>
>     p.lead: Write a rule once and read it in eight SIEM languages. Test it against real log lines before it goes anywhere near production. Everything runs on this machine — nothing is uploaded, and there is nothing to install.
>     buttons: Open a worked example (primary), Start from nothing
>     p.note: New to this? Take the example. It is a real credential-access rule, already filled in, and you can watch it change language as you switch the dialect above.
>   aside.code-card (the live preview)
>     header: dots + rule id + LOCAL badge
>     tabs: 4 dialects (Sigma, Splunk SPL, Sentinel KQL, QRadar AQL) — actually use state.cache.dialects ready ones, first 4? Screenshot shows 4 tabs. Use ready dialects, all 8 might overflow; show first 5 and scroll. I'll show ready dialects in a scrollable tab row.
>     pre#home-code
>     footer: ✓ PARSED ✓ EXPLAINED ✓ RENDERED ... "Eight dialects · refusals named, never guessed"
> section.stats: 8 SIEM DIALECTS / 0 DEPENDENCIES / 4 WORKFLOWS / 100% LOCAL — NOTHING UPLOADED
>    - dialects count live from cache
>    - dependencies 0 (true: stdlib only)
>    - workflows 4 (author, verify, explain, draft) — count from TOOLS groups? Just 4.
> section.workflow: THE WORKFLOW / FOUR THINGS, IN THE ORDER YOU NEED THEM
>    cards: 1 Author → Author step; 2 Test; 3 Evidence (datasets+receipts); 4 Handoff (preview/reference)? 
>    Better aligned to real app:

>    2. Test — three verdicts against your own lines → test
>    3. Keep the evidence — datasets, receipts, history → datasets

> footer line with /classic link, health

      """The rebuilt front end's contract with itself.
      
      There is no DOM in this suite, so these tests protect the things that can be
      checked from bytes on disk -- and those are exactly the things that rot
      silently: a screen that is not wired, a colour that bypasses the token system, a
      control the redesign quietly dropped, and a template that no longer parses.
      
      The behavioural checks (a click produces the right request) live in the manual

                  used |= set(re.findall(r"var\((--[a-z0-9-]+)", read(path)))

              self.assertEqual(missing, [], f"undefined custom properties: {missing}")

              self.assertEqual(len(re.findall(r"(?m)^:root\b", read(TOKENS))), 1)

      class NoMarkupFromStrings(unittest.TestCase):
          def test_the_ui_builds_nodes_never_markup(self):
              """A rule title is user text. Building screens with innerHTML would put
              it in the document as markup. Every node is created with createElement."""
              # Usage, not mention: the rule is stated in prose in dom.js, and prose
              # must be allowed to name the thing it forbids.
              forbidden = [
                  r"\.innerHTML\s*=",
                  r"\binnerHTML\s*\+?=",
                  r"\.outerHTML\s*=",
                  r"insertAdjacentHTML\s*\(",
                  r"document\.write\s*\(",

              sources = list(JS.rglob("*.js"))
              self.assertTrue(sources)
              for path in sorted(sources):
                  source = read(path)
                  for pattern in forbidden:
                      with self.subTest(file=path.name, pattern=pattern):
                          self.assertIsNone(re.search(pattern, source))

              new = read(SHELL) + all_js()

              }

          def test_the_retired_list_is_not_a_wish_list(self):

              old = set(re.findall(r'\bid="([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)"', read(CLASSIC)))

      class Templates(unittest.TestCase):
          def test_templates_are_parsed_by_the_engine_they_rely_on(self):
              """A template that no longer lowers is worse than no template."""
              from web.api import Api
      
              source = read(JS / "core" / "ir.js")

              dialect = re.findall(r"dialect: '([a-z]+)'", block)
              texts = re.findall(r"text: \[(.*?)\]\.join\('\\n'\)", block, re.S)
              self.assertEqual(len(dialect), 4)

      async function loadTemplate(template) {
        await attempt(async () => {
          const data = await api.lower(template.dialect, template.text, template.id);
          loadRule({
            payload: data.rule,
            provenance: template.dialect,
            origin: 'authored',
            sourceText: template.text,
            entryId: null,
            parentId: null,
          });
          state.ui.target = template.dialect;
          if (data.diagnostics && data.diagnostics.length) {
            toast(data.diagnostics.length + ' thing(s) in this template could not be ' +
              'represented. They are listed on Preview.', 'bad');
          } else {
            toast('"' + template.title + '" is loaded. Press Next to walk through it.', 'good');
          }

          rerender();

        }

             it overwrite the full list made the rail count and the Versions screen
             disagree with the store. */
          state.cache.recent = data.entries || [];
          rerender();
        }, { context: 'start' });
      }

- path: web\static\js\core\state.js
  content: |
      /* The one state object.
      
         The DOM never owns truth. Every edit lands here first, and the screen is
         redrawn from here. `mutate` is for typing (state changes, screen does not
         re-render, so the caret stays put); `act` is for buttons (state changes and
         the screen is redrawn). */
      
      import { emptyRule } from './ir.js';
      
      const DRAFT_KEY = 'ruleforge.draft.v1';
      const DRAFT_VERSION = 1;
      
      export const state = {
        doc: {
          payload: emptyRule(),   // exactly what the API calls `rule`
          ruleId: 'draft',
          provenance: 'sentinel', // the dialect it came FROM
          entryId: null,
          parentId: null,
          origin: 'authored',
          sourceText: '',
          sample: { text: '', format: 'jsonl' },
        },
        ui: {
          screen: 'start',
          target: 'sentinel',
          dirty: false,
          busy: false,
          edits: 0,
          problems: [],
          lastRequest: null,
          lastResponse: null,
          inspected: null,
          paletteOpen: false,
          inspectorOpen: false,
        },
        status: { health: null, lastVerdict: null, ruleHash: null, datasetHash: null },
        cache: {
          dialects: [],
          datasets: [],
          runs: [],
          versions: [],
        },
        draftSavedAt: null,
      };
      
      let renderer = () => {};
      const chromeListeners = [];
      
      export function setRenderer(fn) {
        renderer = fn;
      }
      
      export function onChrome(fn) {
        chromeListeners.push(fn);
      }
      
      function persist() {
        try {
          localStorage.setItem(DRAFT_KEY, JSON.stringify({
            v: DRAFT_VERSION,
            at: new Date().toISOString(),
            doc: state.doc,
            target: state.ui.target,
          }));
          state.draftSavedAt = new Date().toISOString();
        } catch (err) {
          /* A full or blocked localStorage must not break editing. The draft is a
             convenience; the engine's store is the record. */
        }
      }
      
      let persistTimer = null;
      function schedulePersist() {
        if (persistTimer) clearTimeout(persistTimer);
        persistTimer = setTimeout(() => {
          persistTimer = null;
          persist();
        }, 400);
      }
